f4b4bb981e:81c4d8fc42e3bb92.title: Insects Girl Cronicles
f4b4bb981e:81c4d8fc42e3bb92.summary: In this series, I combined the forms and vitality of insects with the image of the girl. Like insects, which may appear small and fragile yet possess intricate structures and unique ways of surviving, the girls in these works also carry an unfamiliar strength and sense of combativeness beneath their soft appearances. Dragonfly wings, the colors and movements of bees, and the sharp forms of praying mantises are transformed into the girls' clothing, poses, weapons, and overall atmosphere. Through the image of the girl, these works explore the coexistence of fragility and strength, beauty and threat.

f4b4bb981e:8e267423a3de45cd.title: Zerikusi · Visual identity & website
f4b4bb981e:8e267423a3de45cd.summary: In Basque, Zerikusi means "relationship, bond or connection", but literally translates as "what to see". Two meanings that reflect its approach to communication: connecting ideas and people through messages that are meaningful and bring value. To shape the concept, we draw inspiration from the expression "seeing is believing", highlighting the importance of observing, questioning and understanding before communicating. Because only by asking the right questions can we look beyond the obvious and communicate what truly matters. The exclamation mark represents that moment when something captures our attention and invites us to see things from a different perspective. Zerikusi® is an invitation to question in order to connect and communicate with purpose.

f4b4bb981e:5cfad72d0581f201.title: ZILART Museum
f4b4bb981e:5cfad72d0581f201.summary: ZILART is a new museum of contemporary art in Moscow. Its building is a copper-clad cube with carefully balanced proportions, measuring 60 × 60 meters at its base and rising 36 meters high. The museum's visual voice is a custom typeface, ZILART, defined by asymmetric proportions and an expressive rhythm. Designed with the museum's architectural scale in mind, it works across Cyrillic and Latin scripts, from the logo to typography on copper and concrete surfaces, posters, and digital screens. The identity becomes part of the museum's architecture through large-scale typography, gallery numbers conceived as sculptural objects, wayfinding, entrance design, and digital displays. Mint and deep green create a counterpoint to the warm copper facade, while graphite and natural tones complement the building's materiality. For the museum shop, Collection, we developed a range of publications and objects, including collaborations with contemporary artists.

f4b4bb981e:36e78103bbe0d863.title: OASE : A new skincare system for Mars
f4b4bb981e:36e78103bbe0d863.summary: On Mars, skin spends most of the day sealed inside a suit. Weeks of friction and repeated irritation leave a barrier that has no time to recover. OASE is a speculative skincare brand for the first settlers on Mars. Instead of prescribing products for a fixed skin type, it tracks how skin responds as people move between the airlock, living quarters and sleep pods, and adjusts care as those responses change. The name comes from oasis. Mars once held water, and traces of it still remain in its rock. OASE takes that idea as its premise: a small source of care in an environment that offers none. Care runs on the O.A.S.I.S. protocol, a five-step cycle (Observe, Assess, Separate, Invigorate, Sync) that begins again once it ends. It is delivered through a single kit that combines a smart mirror, a skincare device and four cosmetic products. f4b4bb981e:f4219e26c2845ba2.title: El Capricho de Gaudí
f4b4bb981e:f4219e26c2845ba2.summary: El Capricho, also known as Villa Quijano, is one of the few buildings Antoni Gaudí completed outside Catalonia. Built in Comillas between 1883 and 1885 for Máximo Díaz de Quijano, it is laid out to follow the sun from room to room, which earned it the nickname of the architectural sunflower. Today it is run as a cultural space that welcomes thousands of visitors a month, from families and school groups to international tourists. Its image had not kept pace with that role. The brand needed to work across tickets, signage, workshops, merchandise, digital channels and the building's 140th anniversary, and it had to do so without ever competing with the building it represents. The question was how to change the image of a Gaudí building, and who should be part of that decision.

Local Local cherishes every moment of pause, capturing instances that transcend daily routines, and preparing for future moments of sudden inspiration. The only limit here is the prohibition against stopping your imagination. It's a space for every free spirit to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle that is true to the present, inspiring the now, and can be enjoyed anytime, anywhere. We aim to create an urban inspiration capsule with a sense of city environment awareness and cultural consciousness.

f4b4bb981e:c51e5baede298a64.title: Città di Ancona
f4b4bb981e:c51e5baede298a64.summary: Ancona was born from geography: a promontory that bends into the sea, a natural feature that the ancients recognized and called "Ankón," the "elbow" of Italy. It is a shape that embodies both function and metaphor: shelter and openness, protection and horizon.

a4977d3fa4:641d83ab5cad244c.title: 'Obsession' Director Curry Barker Unveils New Horror Short Film 'Mama Bear'
a4977d3fa4:641d83ab5cad244c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:641d83ab5cad244c.summary: Summary Filmmaker Curry Barker has released a new horror short film titled 'Mama Bear' exclusively on YouTubeThe project marks Barker's first post-'Obsession' release following the horror film's $519 million USD worldwide theatrical runThe director is also preparing his upcoming 2027 feature film 'Anything But Ghosts' starring Aaron Paul and Bryce Dallas Howard Filmmaker Curry Barker has officially debuted his new horror short film Mama Bear, marking his first directorial release since his breakout box-office phenomenon Obsession. The surprise project premiered exclusively on YouTube in partnership with Windows just in time for Halloween.The short film arrives on the heels of the historic theatrical run of Obsession, which grossed $519 million USD worldwide on a sub-$1 million USD production budget. Audiences quickly drew thematic connections between the title of 'Mama Bear' and Barker's debut feature, referencing the lead character Bear (portrayed by Michael Johnston) and co-star Inde Navarrette, who earned critical acclaim and Oscar buzz before joining Marvel's X-Men reboot as Rogue.Following the success of Obsession, Barker secured an eight-figure deal with Universal and Blumhouse and is currently readying his upcoming horror-comedy feature, Anything But Ghosts, scheduled to hit theaters on May 7, 2027, through Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster. Co-written with and starring longtime collaborator Cooper Tomlinson alongside Aaron Paul, Bryce Dallas Howard, Violet McGraw, and Chris Reinacher, the project follows amateur paranormal investigators.Curry Barker's Mama Bear is currently available to stream exclusively on YouTube. First reported by Mason Tiniuc, the silhouette forms one half of a two-piece November pack alongside the low-top Badbo 1.1, continuing the Puerto Rican artist’s affinity for muted, neutral color palettes.The sneaker is defined by its tonal textural contrast, layering rich "Grey Three" suede overlays across a premium "Orbit Grey" leather base. Rather than relying on bold color blocking, the closely matched tones allow the tactile variation between the smooth leather underlays and the fuzzy suede panels to take center stage. The tongue preserves the hallmark zigzag stitching that has become a defining characteristic of the Badbo 1.0 silhouette. a4977d3fa4:065709d7d37a3f9f.title: Kojima Productions Drops the Visceral First Trailer for ‘DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS'
a4977d3fa4:065709d7d37a3f9f.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:065709d7d37a3f9f.summary: Summary Death Stranding Isolations has dropped its first teaser trailer.The anime follows a new girl and other original characters living in Sam Bridges’ reconnected world.The Disney+ series premieres in 2027. “My mom became a crater.” With that bleak declaration, DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS offers its first proper look at the animated world expanding beyond Hideo Kojima’s games. The newly released teaser trailer shifts attention away from Sam Bridges and toward an unnamed young girl who lost her mother to the Death Stranding, leaving her to grow accustomed to a life of isolation.Rendered in E&H production’s hand-drawn 2D style, the footage moves through desolate North American landscapes and glimpses of the new characters whose lives will eventually intersect: a boy consumed by anger, a female soldier trapped in a cycle of conflict and an older man seeking his own way of connecting people. The girl remains the emotional center of the preview, with an unexpected encounter seemingly pulling her away from the solitary existence she has chosen and into a much larger journey.First announced at the Disney+ Originals Preview in Hong Kong in November 2025, DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS is set immediately after Sam reconnects North America through the Chiral Network, exploring the unforeseen consequences of bringing a fractured society back together. Hideo Kojima serves as executive producer, with Takayuki Sano directing and Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045 artist Ilya Kuvshinov providing original character designs; the latest update also confirms Mardock Scramble author Tow Ubukata as series composition and screenplay writer.Watch the first teaser trailer above. DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS is confirmed to stream exclusively on Disney+ sometime 2027. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Hideo Kojima (@hideo_kojima) Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:1b6d706de7e51bac.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)

a4977d3fa4:ce30e3494a58a66e.title: Sir Patrick Stewart, Legendary 'Star Trek' Captain and 'X-Men' Icon, Dies at 86
a4977d3fa4:ce30e3494a58a66e.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ce30e3494a58a66e.summary: Summary Acclaimed British stage and screen actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86The performer was celebrated globally for his defining portrayals of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in X-MenStewart passed away at his home in Los Angeles following a journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia Legendary British stage and screen actor Sir Patrick Stewart, iconic for his portrayals of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise, has died at the age of 86. Stewart passed away Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles following a journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.Born in Mirfield, Yorkshire, Stewart established his early career with the Royal Shakespeare Company and the National Theatre before transitioning to American screen stardom. In 1987, he took command of the U.S.S. Enterprise as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, leading the beloved sci-fi series across seven seasons and four subsequent feature films before returning to the role in 2020's Star Trek: Picard. In 2000, Stewart originated the role of Professor Charles Xavier in Marvel's groundbreaking X-Men, anchoring the franchise through seminal entries including X2, Days of Future Past, and Logan, while also filming an appearance for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.Beyond sci-fi, Stewart was an accomplished performer with notable roles in Excalibur, David Lynch's Dune, and American Dad!, alongside acclaimed stage and television turns that earned him multiple Emmy and Golden Globe nominations. He was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 2001 and was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010. Remembered for infusing his characters with enduring dignity, compassion, and intellect, Stewart is survived by his wife, Sunny Ozell, and his two children, Daniel and Sophia. Fashion heads naturally stayed true to form, with one guy hunting down a "really faded Twisted Sister shirt," while our own Eric spotted a military Humvee parked on the curb and admitted on the spot, "Dude, I would buy that right there!"The humor kept rolling as we chatted with different crowds across the block. When asked what he'd do first, one local hit back with an eco-agrarian route, laughing, "Buy a couple cows, got some chickens... and I'm a millionaire!" Meanwhile, one boyfriend casually mapped out his math: "75 million in the stock market” while the rest goes to his partner as she comically asks, “to me?”. He politely and smartly abides. From a guy planning an "Alaskan kickback" to a cosplayer traveling the world for conventions and someone wanting to open an open-water survival swim school, the energy was pure, unfiltered joy.That fun, unscripted vibe is exactly the point of the campaign. a4977d3fa4:793004096e49de50.title: Pedro Pascal Conducts Tony Gilroy's 'Behemoth!' in Director's First Film in 14 Years
a4977d3fa4:793004096e49de50.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:793004096e49de50.summary: Summary Tony Gilroy has unveiled the official trailer for Behemoth! starring Pedro Pascal as a cellist scoring films in Los AngelesThe nonlinear narrative features original compositions from nine acclaimed composers including Michael Giacchino and Alan SilvestriThe ensemble cast stars Olivia Wilde alongside Will Arnett and Matthew Lillard marking Gilroy's first feature film in 14 years Filmmaker Tony Gilroy has officially unveiled the trailer for his upcoming drama Behemoth!, starring Pedro Pascal as a classical cellist returning to Los Angeles to score motion pictures. The project marks the director’s first feature film in 14 years following a celebrated reception at the New York Film Festival.The formally ambitious, character-driven narrative chronicles two decades in the life of cellist Alex Serian (Pascal), exploring the unresolved reasons behind his departure and return. Constructed around a nonlinear, music-led framework where musical cues trigger memories spanning 20 years, the film consistently intercuts between live orchestral performances and Alex’s real life. Rather than serving as passive background accompaniment, the score functions as an active narrative device reflecting his personal turning points.To establish the film's complex musical architecture, Gilroy enlisted nine distinct composers—Michael Giacchino, Alan Silvestri, James Newton Howard, Michael Abels, Henry Jackman, Emily Bear, Lukas Frank, Nami Melumad, and Brandon Roberts—each scoring a different fictional movie within the story. The ensemble cast features Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Alexa Swinton, Will Arnett, and Matthew Lillard, arriving as Gilroy’s first feature since 2012’s The Bourne Legacy and his acclaimed tenure helming Andor.Behemoth! premieres in theaters on December 4. a4977d3fa4:6944ac6972d3ab53.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:6944ac6972d3ab53.summary: With its founding philosophy, a Sound Mind in a Sound Body, ASICS has stood as an unwavering champion of movement for the mind. Feeding into events and activations, this year on World Mental Health Day, the brand installed a life-sized diorama in Paris showing its commitment to tackling issues humanity faces today. Boxed in a see-through case, the diorama centered on a realistic human model, sitting in a familiar position in front of screens, immobile and hunched over. From a global study stating 86% of people surveyed spend their waking hours inactive, it captured one of the most widespread modern behaviors. ASICS presented the model as part of a new species it calls Homo Scrollus Canapus. Though it takes a humorous side, the installation adopted a museum format with explanatory labels and documentary-style voiceovers to engage those passing by. Hypebeast visited the forecourt of Grande Halle de La Villette, which housed the diorama for two days. Positioned in the middle of a high-traffic area, we went on the ground to catch individuals as they interacted with the installation. The video shows all walks of life observing the model and sharing personal stories of the modern-day habits that have quietly designed movement out of our lives, like doomscrolling, binge-watching, and prolonged hours in front of computer screens.The diorama, however, wasn’t just a warning of the new species. It gave onlookers a solution to kicking their restless slump to the curb. On one side of the installation, a board noted that dedicating a few minutes to movement can boost your mind and body. These insights were championed by its 15 Minutes to Thrive challenge. Aiming to encourage everyday activity, we gathered perspectives on the initiative in a dedicated Ask the Community installment. a4977d3fa4:28ee339697c06f8a.title: 'Pokémon Unite' to Officially Shut Down in March 2027
a4977d3fa4:28ee339697c06f8a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:28ee339697c06f8a.summary: Summary The Pokémon Company has announced that 'Pokémon Unite' will officially conclude service on March 23 2027Developed with TiMi Studios the five-on-five MOBA has halted gem purchases and auto-renewals ahead of a final farewell event in NovemberA newly introduced Library feature will allow players to download and view select in-game items locally before servers go offline The Pokémon Company has confirmed that Pokémon Unite will officially shut down in March 2027. The five-on-five multiplayer online battle arena title will close its servers on March 23, 2027, at 00:00 UTC (March 22 at 8:00 PM ET), concluding a nearly six-year live-service run.Developed alongside Tencent’s TiMi Studios, the free-to-play MOBA originally launched on Nintendo Switch in July 2021 before rolling out to mobile devices with full cross-platform matchmaking. The impending shutdown follows an earlier indication in July, when The Pokémon Company removed the title from the 2027 Pokémon World Championships in favor of an independent Tokyo tournament that will begin qualifiers this December.With the closure announced, in-game sales of gems, new Unite Club memberships, and subscription auto-renewals have been terminated immediately. Players can continue spending previously acquired gems until the final cutoff, and existing memberships will remain active through their standard expiration dates. a4977d3fa4:222cb81a65fef6fc.title: Milwaukee Brewers Win First World Series Title in Franchise History
a4977d3fa4:222cb81a65fef6fc.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:222cb81a65fef6fc.summary: Summary The Milwaukee Brewers have captured their first World Series title in franchise history by defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in five gamesManager Pat Murphy and captain Christian Yelich led the squad through an 11-2 postseason run following a franchise-record 103 regular-season winsThe historic victory caps a 58-year journey for the organization dating back to its 1969 origins as the Seattle Pilots The Milwaukee Brewers have officially clinched their first MLB World Series championship in franchise history, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games during the 123rd Fall Classic. The victory at Tropicana Field concludes a dominant 11-2 postseason run and brings an end to a 58-year title drought.Under manager Pat Murphy and president of baseball operations Matt Arnold, the Brewers translated a franchise-record 103 regular-season victories into an unstoppable October surge. Milwaukee dismantled the San Diego Padres in four games and swept the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS before vanquishing Tampa Bay, closing their campaign on a remarkable 26-5 stretch dating back to September.Anchored by the clubhouse leadership of captain Christian Yelich and pitcher Brandon Woodruff, the championship squad paired experienced guidance with a dynamic young core featuring Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang, and Jacob Misiorowski. On the field, Milwaukee paced the majors in batting average, on-base percentage, and walk rate while holding top-two league rankings in team ERA and strikeout percentage.The triumph marks the franchise’s first world championship since its 1969 inception as the Seattle Pilots and subsequent move to Wisconsin in 1970, eclipsing the legacy of the 1982 pennant-winning squad to permanently etch the club into baseball history. a4977d3fa4:c7417cd19963f61b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:c7417cd19963f61b.summary: Summary he British Fashion Council has announced that Yohji Yamamoto will receive the Outstanding Achievement Award at the Fashion Awards 2026The honor recognizes the Japanese designer's radical approach to tailoring and over five decades of creative influence across fashion and artThe ceremony is scheduled to take place on November 30 at London's Royal Albert Hall Yohji Yamamoto will be honored with the Outstanding Achievement Award by the British Fashion Council at the upcoming Fashion Awards 2026. The accolade celebrates the legendary Japanese designer's extensive contributions to the global fashion landscape and his lasting impact across generations of designers.Since establishing his namesake label in Tokyo in 1972, Yamamoto has remained a transformative force in contemporary design, celebrated for his intellectual ethos, masterful tailoring, and radical reinterpretation of womenswear. Beyond his core lines, Yamamoto’s influence extends into costuming for film and opera alongside Y-3, his groundbreaking collaborative venture with adidas inaugurated in 2003. Addressing the honor, British Fashion Council chief executive officer Laura Weir remarked, “Few designers have changed the way we think about clothes as profoundly as Yamamoto. His work has always challenged convention while remaining deeply rooted in craft, precision and an uncompromising creative vision.”Yamamoto joins a celebrated roster of prior honorees including Karl Lagerfeld, Miuccia Prada, Giorgio Armani, Ralph Lauren, and Tom Ford. The ceremony will also recognize Jimmy Choo’s Sandra Choi with a Special Recognition Award alongside top honors like Designer of the Year.The Fashion Awards 2026 will take place on November 30 at London’s Royal Albert Hall. a4977d3fa4:ae02b76ce75d2a5c.title: Lydia Yee Spells Out Southeast Asian Art, From A to Z
a4977d3fa4:ae02b76ce75d2a5c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ae02b76ce75d2a5c.summary: Kuala Lumpur started at Medan Pasar, the old market square where the Gombak and Klang rivers meet. Along its western edge stand six Art Deco shophouses from the 1930s, home to traditional merchants before banks and finance houses moved in during the 1960s. On November 1, they open their doors again as Muara Arts, a roughly 20,000-square-foot not-for-profit gallery for Malaysian and Southeast Asian modern and contemporary art, and the first institution of its kind in the country.The project belongs to Shanthi Kandiah and Brahmal Vasudevan, founders of the Creador Foundation, with the restored buildings designed by Dr. Tan LM and Sean Carpenter of Linear Vista. Muara is Malay for estuary, and the founders credit the name to “the late Valentine Willie, who was a consultant to us and spent his career connecting artists across Southeast Asia and showing their work side by side.” Staying not-for-profit is central to the idea, they say, because it “means the gallery exists for artists and the public, not the market.”Setting the program is Lydia Yee, Muara’s Consultant Artistic Director and the former Chief Curator of London’s Whitechapel Gallery, whose three-decade career also runs through the Barbican Art Gallery and The Bronx Museum of the Arts. Some of the artists she’s now showing in Kuala Lumpur are old acquaintances. “My relationship with some of the artists actually goes back to the 1990s,” she says. “Pacita Abad exhibited at the Bronx Museum of the Arts and I helped acquire her work for the museum’s collection. I know Paul Pfeiffer from the artist collective Godzilla and the Whitney Independent Study Program in New York.” Alongside those relationships, she has tried to bring “the necessary procedures and policies for exhibition making, while leaving behind a prescriptive institutional mentality.”Abad and Pfeiffer both feature in Muara’s opening exhibition, "A–Z of Southeast Asian Art: A Critical Dictionary," co-curated by Yee and Zhen Feng Ang. a4977d3fa4:d75c998c39a6b56b.summary: Summary Netflix has unveiled the official debut trailer for its upcoming limited series adaptation of 'Pride and Prejudice'Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden lead the cast as Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy alongside Olivia Colman and Rufus SewellThe six-part production is scripted by Dolly Alderton and directed by Heartstopper filmmaker Euros Lyn Netflix has officially released the first trailer for its upcoming limited series Pride and Prejudice, starring Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden. The six-part production brings Jane Austen’s classic 1813 romantic drama back to the screen.Penned by Everything I Know About Love author Dolly Alderton and directed by Heartstopper filmmaker Euros Lyn, the six-part limited series follows the will-they-won’t-they dynamic between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy as they navigate the rigid societal landscape of 19th-century England. Produced by Lisa Osborne, the project is executive produced by Corrin, Alderton, and Lyn alongside Laura Lankester, as well as Will Johnston and Louise Mutter for Lookout Point.The ensemble cast features Olivia Colman as Mrs. Bennet, Rufus Sewell as Mr. Bennet, Freya Mavor as Jane Bennet, Jamie Demetriou as Mr. Collins, and Daryl McCormack as Mr. Bingley. Rounding out the lineup are Louis Partridge as Mr. Wickham, Rhea Norwood as Lydia Bennet, Siena Kelly as Caroline Bingley, and Fiona Shaw as Lady Catherine de Bourg. Screen newcomers Hopey Parish and Hollie Avery make their debuts as Mary Bennet and Kitty Bennet, joined by supporting cast members Anjana Vasan, Sebastian Armesto, Rosie Cavaliero, Saffron Coomber, James Dryden, Justin Edwards, James Northcote, Eloise Webb, and Isabella Sermon.Pride and Prejudice premieres on Netflix on December 3. a4977d3fa4:8ffce0e5bcc19065.summary: Summary New York-based photographer Adam Powell will present his first solo exhibition at Tokyo's DIESEL ART GALLERYTitled 'The DESERT is a CIRCLE,' the show features photographs from recent years, of motels, landscapes, and portraits, many of which shot across ArizonaThe exhibition will run until January 11, 2027 What do Cameron Winters, Eric Adams, and Diesel have in common? They’re among the many faces and brands that have passed through Adam Powell’s lens, and if you don’t know the New York-based photographer, you might recognize a few of his editorial spreads or campaigns from a wide-ranging client list. His career has taken him all over, but the gallery space is still a first.Diesel Art Gallery will host the debut solo exhibition by Powell at its Tokyo space from November 14 through January 11. Days blur together in shots that span majestic landscapes and surreal self-portraits, drifting between reality and fantasy. The exhibition runs from November 14 through January 11, 2027. a4977d3fa4:b445fe95a30bf735.title: Netflix Examines College Title IX Accountability in 'Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell'
a4977d3fa4:b445fe95a30bf735.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b445fe95a30bf735.summary: Summary Netflix has revealed the latest installment of its quick-turn documentary series titled 'Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell'The investigative project examines university Title IX proceedings and campus safety following a student lawsuit against the institutionFeaturing interviews with New York Governor Kathy Hochul and student journalists the film is scheduled to premiere on October 29 Netflix has officially announced its upcoming investigative release, Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell. The quick-turn documentary examines the institutional fallout of a high-profile campus sexual assault lawsuit and scrutinizes university Title IX systems.The documentary centers on the legal action brought by Jane Doe, a former Cornell University student who alleges she was drugged and raped at the school's Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024. As the incident sparked widespread campus protests and intensified national scrutiny surrounding collegiate accountability, the film investigates whether institutional reporting mechanisms, specifically campus police and Title IX offices, deliver on their intended promise of protection and due process.Produced by Words + Pictures with Steve Yaccino serving as showrunner, the installment features interviews with New York Governor Kathy Hochul, Jane Doe's attorney Thomas Giuffra, and former Brown University Title IX coordinator Amanda Walsh. The narrative also incorporates firsthand insights from The Cornell Daily Sun editor-in-chief Sophia Dasser, senior editor Cereese Qusba, a former fraternity president, and a recent alumna who navigated the school's Title IX procedures.Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell, the fifth installment in the streamer's ongoing series, premieres on Netflix on October 29, 2026. Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:50fa1fe2ec6355f0.title: You Can Now Spend the Night at a Jean Prouvè-Designed Home
a4977d3fa4:50fa1fe2ec6355f0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:50fa1fe2ec6355f0.summary: A Modernist home designed by Jean Prouvè and his son Claude has been restored and transformed into a guesthouse, offering a chance to stay inside an architectural gem. The home, named Maison Prouvè 58, is located near the French village of Saint-Paul-de-Vence – an area once known as a creative haven for artists and writers, filled with galleries and museums. A rare example of mid-century French prefabricated architecture, it was completed back in 1958, and marked the first collaboration between Prouvè and his son. Its distinctly modernist exterior sees huge windows run the length of one side of the building, looking out onto the surrounding Mediterranean landscape. Inside, the house is organised around a central corridor – one side leads to two bedrooms a playroom, and a bathroom. The other opens out on to the communal areas, a kitchen, dining area and living room. Not only would you be living within a slice of architectural history, you'd be living amongst objects equally as significant. Furniture throughout has been chosen to complement the building, and brings together some of the most influential figures of 20th century design, including the likes of Charlotte Perriand, Pierre Jeanneret and Le Corbusier. Bookings for Maison Prouvè are now being taken. You can find out more on the agency website. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:8ba3d5807b9556c0.title: Maison Margiela and NUDAKE Serve Tea With a Deconstructed Twist
a4977d3fa4:8ba3d5807b9556c0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:8ba3d5807b9556c0.summary: Summary Maison Margiela and NUDAKE reinterpret tea rituals through deconstructed porcelain and shared forms.Bianchetto finishes, warped rims and joined saucers define the “OOPS” aesthetic.The collection launches October 30 at NUDAKE TEAHOUSE in Seoul. Maison Margiela and NUDAKE are turning tea time into an exercise in controlled imperfection. Dubbed “OOPS,” the pair’s first collaboration takes the Maison’s deconstructive codes away from fashion and applies them to porcelain, tea and the ritual of sharing a pot.Much of the collection is washed in Margiela’s signature Bianchetto treatment, giving otherwise familiar tea objects a deliberately unfinished, timeworn character. A sculptural teapot anchors the range with a metal ring at its lid and the house’s recognizable four-stitch detail pressed into its body, while accompanying cups distort the expected symmetry of traditional teaware through gently warped rims and a joined double saucer intended for two.That idea of two people sharing one experience runs through more than the ceramics. NUDAKE’s accompanying Oops black tea takes inspiration from the image of a dark crimson plum being crushed beneath a leather shoe, translating the scene into a blend layered with delicate herbs, sweet fruit and earthy notes. a4977d3fa4:0265a83b05af5e43.title: Japanese Artisans Rework Vintage Polo Ralph Lauren for Reimagined Collection at PoloFest Tokyo
a4977d3fa4:0265a83b05af5e43.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:0265a83b05af5e43.summary: Summary Polo Ralph Lauren has showcased its Reimagined collection at the inaugural PoloFest celebration in TokyoJapanese craftspeople including Yui Narita and Mitsugu Sasaki utilized traditional boro mending and embroidery across archival Polo silhouettesEach reworked piece is offered through a charity raffle with all proceeds benefiting Ralph Lauren's Pink Pony cancer initiative Polo Ralph Lauren has officially presented its one-of-a-kind "Reimagined" collection during the inaugural PoloFest activation in Tokyo. The installation brings together prominent Japanese artisans to breathe new life into vintage Polo garments using traditional mending and restoration techniques.The collection repurposes pre-worn garments into tactile, textured works of art. Key pieces on display include classic chinos embroidered with smiley face emoji patterns, heavily patchworked ties and hats rebuilt with layered fabric scraps, and distressed denim baseball caps stitched with individual red felt letters spelling out "RALPH." The initiative highlights master craftspeople such as Yui Narita, founder of Osaka vintage store Brown Tabby Works, alongside Mitsugu Sasaki of Sasaki Yōhinten, who applied the traditional Japanese practice of boro to repair and reinforce garments through hand-sewn fabric layering.The showcase directly reflects Ralph Lauren’s personal reverence for well-loved clothing, echoing the designer's philosophy that "where wear becomes character, repair becomes art, and every stitch creates a new patina." Serving as the opening activation ahead of the brand's 60th anniversary in 2027, the three-day PoloFest gathering honors Japan’s longstanding connection to the label since its arrival in 1976, celebrating decades of local craftsmanship and classic Americana.The Polo Ralph Lauren Reimagined pieces are available exclusively via charity raffle at PoloFest Tokyo, with all proceeds directly supporting the Pink Pony initiative to fight cancer. a4977d3fa4:fa2575444596f9d4.title: Instagram Challenges YouTube With New 90-Minute Longform Video Uploads
a4977d3fa4:fa2575444596f9d4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fa2575444596f9d4.summary: Summary Instagram has begun testing a new upload format dubbed Features allowing creators to share longform videos up to 90 minutes in lengthThe initiative aims to connect short-form Reels with in-depth video content optimized for mobile viewing and the Instagram TV appCurrently undergoing trials in Brazil the test is slated to expand to select creators across the United States Instagram has officially begun testing "Features", a new upload format enabling creators to share longform videos up to 90 minutes in length. The move marks a strategic shift toward extended media after years of prioritizing short-form video.The feature represents Instagram’s most notable longform endeavor since sunsetting IGTV. Explaining the pivot, Instagram VP of Product Tessa Lyons noted, "Reels is still going to be a core part of Instagram. But when you want to go deeper with the creators you love and the content that they’re creating, you should be able to do that on Instagram.” To build an interconnected system, the platform is testing "Clips as Reels," allowing creators to turn snippets into links pointing to full-length uploads, alongside options to push playback directly to the Instagram TV app.Addressing the strategy, Instagram head Adam Mosseri shared, “The thing that the team has been working on that we’re excited to share with you is trying to make it so that the short-form and the long-form video can be symbiotic. We’re going to try to support these different types of formats, both in the mobile app, but also on the TV app... I’m actually very excited about it, and we’re very committed to it long term.”Currently undergoing trials in Brazil, testing for "Features" and "Clips as Reels" will soon expand to select creators across the United States. d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.title: The New Energy Stalemate in Ukraine
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.author: Tatiana Mitrova, Sergey Vakulenko
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.summary: Tatiana Mitrova, a fellow at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy and former energy scholar at Moscow’s Russian Academy of Sciences, and Sergey Vakulenko, an oil and gas expert at Carnegie’s Russia Eurasia Center, argue that Russia and Ukraine are locked in an energy war that has become an adaptation spiral, despite growing human and economic costs and despite current US pressure on Ukraine. They observe Ukraine’s remarkable ability to withstand Russian strikes, while questioning claims that long-range Ukrainian strikes will be able to achieve game-changing damage on Russia. Ukraine and Russia have transformed the role of energy warfare in modern conflict, drawing on low costs drones but also new forms of technological resilience that are likely to make wars longer and more dangerous.

d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.title: AI Is a Choice
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.author: Alex Imas, Mohamed A. El-Erian, James Manyika
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.summary: Alex Imas, Mohamed El-Erian, and James Manyika, leading voices at the intersection of business and technology, argue that realizing AI’s potential requires giving workers, communities, AI labs, infrastructure developers, and big companies a share of the gains. Using insights from game theory, they argue that increased cooperation can make AI work for all.

d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.title: The China Price
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.author: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.

d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.title: Empires of AI
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.author: Niall Ferguson, Lisa Klaassen, Eric Schmidt
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.summary: In this essay, Niall Ferguson, one of the world’s foremost experts on imperial history, teams up the former CEO of Google, Eric Schmidt, and the researcher Lisa Klaasen to make the provocative argument that AI is an inherently “imperial technology”—and to reveal what the fate of past empires might say about the future of U.S.-Chinese competition in a world shaped by AI.

d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.title: “Earth Satellites and Foreign Policy”
d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.summary: The advent of a new technology invariably comes with strategic implications, raising the question of who will benefit and whether risks can be managed. In 1957, following the Soviet Sputnik launch, U.S. policymakers and analysts recognized that the satellite, as the American physicist and engineer Lloyd Berkner observed in these pages, would bring transformative effects. The United States could not risk losing out, Berkner argued, but nor should governments allow geopolitical tensions to prevent the technology’s broad benefits from emerging.

d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.title: Europe’s Credibility Gap
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.author: Claas Mertens, Ngaire Woods
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.summary: Ngaire Woods, Dean of Oxford’s Blavatnik School of Government, Claas Mertens, also at Oxford, have written a piece arguing that Europe, despite its attempts at self-sufficiency, remains dependent on an unpredictable United States. The continent needs to address this vulnerability so that it can convince other countries, many of which find themselves similarly vulnerable to great-power coercion, that it is a worthy partner.

d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.title: A Better “America First”

d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.author: Andrea Kendall-Taylor, Richard Fontaine
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.summary: Andrea Kendall-Taylor and Richard Fontaine, former members of the National Security Council, argue that the members of what they call the “axis of upheaval”—Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea—are deepening their cooperation. Meanwhile, Washington is creating friction with many of its own partnerships. If these developments continue unabated, the United States will squander the strength of its network just as its adversaries learn to make the most of theirs.

d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.title: The Nuclear Deal That Could Save NATO
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.author: Ivo H. Daalder
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.summary: Former U.S. NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder argues that the scramble to shore up Europe's conventional defense risks overlooking the continent's greatest security weakness: nuclear deterrence. But he lays out a middle path between dependence and nuclearization that would extend France's and the United Kingdom's nuclear umbrella—a course, he argues, that could even repair the transatlantic alliance.

d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.title: The Scramble for the Open Seas
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.author: Michael Albertus
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.summary: Over the last half millennium, societies around the globe competed to divide up the world’s land. Nearly every square inch of soil outside Antarctica is now owned and tucked within national borders. But the oceans have largely been spared that fate. There were times throughout history when countries tried to gate and regulate the seas, but they were too vast to be controlled for long periods. During the Cold War, as technology made it far easier to imagine partitioning the world’s waterways and seabeds, great powers avoided an unrestrained race to grab the oceans. Most governments agreed to deal with them through a patchwork of treaties and multilateral bodies that sought to guarantee freedom of navigation in international waters and assign coastal seabeds to adjacent littoral states.

d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.title: Ideas and Firm Dynamics When It Takes Two to Tango
fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.author: Honghao Wang
fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.summary: Teams of inventors now produce over 80 percent of U.S. patents, up from just 45 percent in 1976. Over the same period, inventor employment has become increasingly concentrated in large firms, rising six times more than overall employment concentration. To explain these trends, we develop a new model of endogenous team formation within firms and embed it in a general equilibrium model of the inventor labor market. Teams increase firms’ returns to scale by increasing the likelihood of productive matches between inventors. The value of these matches rises over time, possibly driven by increasing knowledge specialization. This causes large firms to expand and small firms to shrink in equilibrium, accounting for the observed increase in inventor employment concentration. Because firms do not internalize knowledge spillovers, there is misallocation of inventors across firms. The rise of team production amplifies this misallocation by a factor of six by reallocating inventors away from small firms that generate disproportionately large knowledge spillovers.

fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.title: Relative Development and the Intelligence Divide: Human Capital, Technology Diffusion, and AI
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.author: Jonathan R. W. Temple
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.summary: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help poorer countries catch up? This paper argues that the answer depends less on access to AI than on the capacity to use new knowledge productively. We show that countries have narrowed gaps in capital and schooling more readily than gaps in productivity. Technology can diffuse widely without producing productivity convergence. Measured human capital explains only a modest share of productivity differences in levels, but is associated with sharply different mobility regimes. The estimated transition processes imply an expected time to exit the lowest-productivity state of about 65 years for economies below the estimated human-capital threshold, compared with about 25 years for those above it. This reconciles development accounting with the view of human capital as absorptive capacity. If AI mainly augments skilled workers and capable firms, it may reinforce existing gaps. If it lowers the costs of learning, adaptation, and implementation in weaker-capability economies, it could instead promote convergence. The Intelligence Divide is therefore not simply about access to AI, but about the capacity to turn knowledge into productivity.

fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.title: Growth in Chains: EU Value Chain Productivity and its Slowdown
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.author: Lähdemäki, Sakari
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.summary: Abstract We study Europe’s post-2008 productivity slowdown using novel total factor productivity (TFP) measures that follow production beyond individual industries in global value chains (GVCs). We collect a newset of stylized facts: (1) the slowdown is broad-based, with productivity growth weakening both in final-producer industries and in upstream industries; (2) the staggered entry into force of bilateral investment treaties with China is followed by higher value-chain TFP and greater business-intangible investment; while (3) the gains associated with technology intangibles are weak. We use these facts to discipline a stylized two-region general-equilibrium model with business capabilities, technology-related knowledge, and cross-border knowledge spillovers. The calibration supports a two-stage interpretation of Europe’s experience: (1) sizeable initial integration gains because accumulated business capabilities convert market access into productivity, and (2) later losses when technology improvements are converted into productivity more effectively elsewhere.

fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.title: A Fork in the Road for Global AI Governance: To Repair or Reconfigure Expert-Led Governance?
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.author: Olugbade, Olajide
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a live object of global governance, with expert-led institutional arrangements emerging across an international regime complex. While scholarship on epistemic communities and science-policy interfaces treats expertise as a mechanism for coordination under uncertainty, recent work in Objectual International Relations (O-IR) and Science and Technology Studies foregrounds knowledge politics, contested authority, and the co-productive character of governance. We bring these perspectives into conversation with AI governance through a reflexive workshop design using Nominal Group Technique, drawing on two expert workshops in the UK and US. Findings show that expert panels remain valued for structuring debate, coordinating knowledge, and lending legitimacy to policy action. Yet participants identified tensions around exclusion, elite and private capture, weak accountability, geopolitical constraints, and temporal misalignment between institutional processes and technological change. An object-centered analysis further shows that AI remains an unstable governance object; the knowledge required to govern it is contested and unevenly distributed; and expertise itself is politically charged and institutionally unsettled. We synthesize these tensions into two pathways: Repair and Reconfiguration. Repair seeks to stabilize AI as a governable object, standardize relevant knowledge, and secure expert authority through institutional continuity and procedural refinement. Reconfiguration seeks to keep AI contested, broaden credible forms of knowledge, and reshape expertise through participation, reflexivity, and engagement with politics. The framework provides a critical lens for assessing emerging institutional designs for global AI governance and the trade-offs they entail.

fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.title: From Individual to Social Imitation: How Communities Expand Organizational Search
fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.author: Christopher Tucci
fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.summary: Generative artificial intelligence illustrates a broader organizational puzzle: young, resource-constrained firms can build on knowledge produced across a wider field to address problems that exceed their internal experience. We theorize one mechanism as social imitation: a distributed and recursive process through which communities observe practices and outcomes across organizations, distill recurrent elements into portable strategies, circulate them, and revise the collective repertoire as adoption produces new evidence. This perspective endogenizes the object of imitation. Organizations do not merely copy practices; communities collectively produce what becomes available to copy. We distinguish the source of a candidate (directly observed organizations or a collective) from its mode of adoption (blind or informed), and examine four forms of imitation in an agent-based model of organizational search. Collective sourcing alone does not improve performance. Its value depends on situated evaluation: assessing whether a candidate fits the adopter's configuration. As interdependence increases, informed social imitation improves population performance and the best solution discovered. As problems grow, it becomes more likely to outperform informed imitation from one or several directly observed peers because collective distillation sustains a broader candidate repertoire. Most gains arise from evaluating a small candidate set, and population performance can improve when only a minority of organizations possesses evaluative capability. Social imitation thus reveals a division of cognitive labor: communities expand the strategies organizations can consider, while organizations create value by determining which strategies fit. It explains how firms can mobilize knowledge beyond their boundaries, and why widespread access to collective knowledge does not produce equal benefits.

5b51167fb0:bdb556254e68b6c5.title: Who Marries Whom? The Role of Segregation by Race and Class
5b51167fb0:bdb556254e68b6c5.author: info@aeaweb.org (Benjamin Goldman1, Jamie Gracie2 and Sonya R. Porter3 1 Cornell University (email: bgoldman@cornell.edu) 2 Harvard University (email: jgracie@g.harvard.edu) 3 US Census Bureau…
5b51167fb0:bdb556254e68b6c5.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3623-3673 Abstract Americans rarely marry outside their race or class group, a pattern with well-documented implications for inequality and intergenerational mobility. Limited exposure may partly explain these low intergroup marriage rates. We instrument for exposure using variation in childhood neighborhoods based on whether other race and class groups had more opposite-sex children of similar age. Exposure increases interclass (high- and low-parent income) marriage but has no detectable effect on interracial (White and Black) marriage. A spatial marriage model predicts that residential segregation—one of many forms of exposure—accounts for more than one-third of marital sorting by class but less than 5 percent by race. (JEL J12, J15, J62, R23)

5b51167fb0:b43f16929197f266.title: Taxing Top Wealth: Migration Responses and Their Aggregate Economic Implications
5b51167fb0:b43f16929197f266.author: info@aeaweb.org (Katrine Jakobsen1, Henrik Kleven2, Jonas Kolsrud3, Camille Landais4 and Mathilde Munoz5 1 University of Copenhagen (email: katrinemariejakobsen@gmail.com) 2 Princeton University,…
5b51167fb0:b43f16929197f266.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3674-3720 Abstract Using administrative data from Scandinavian countries, we provide evidence on international migration responses to wealth taxes and evaluate their aggregate economic implications. We find significant migration responses among the wealthy: A 1 percentage point increase in the top wealth tax rate decreases the stock of wealthy taxpayers by about 2 percent. A large fraction of the wealthy are business owners, and their businesses are negatively affected by owner out-migration. The aggregate effects are nevertheless modest: The migration responses to a 1 percentage point increase in the top wealth tax rate reduce employment by 0.02 percent, investments by 0.07 percent, and value added by 0.10 percent. (JEL D31, E22, E24, F22, H24, L26, K34)

5b51167fb0:da85f2a2d1dc685d.title: Racial Promotion Gaps
5b51167fb0:da85f2a2d1dc685d.author: info@aeaweb.org (Deepak Hegde1, Alexander Ljungqvist2 and Manav Raj3 1 New York University and NBER (email: dhegde@stern.nyu.edu) 2 Stockholm School of Economics, Swedish House of Finance, and CEPR…
5b51167fb0:da85f2a2d1dc685d.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3721-3767 Abstract We study racial disparities in promotions in a setting in which promotions are formulaic: the US patent office. Using detailed administrative data that allow us to observe who is eligible for promotion when, we document that Black patent examiners experience delays in promotions they are entitled to, slowing their climb to the top of the career ladder by a year and reducing career earnings by 2.5 percent. Institutional features rule out statistical discrimination with accurate priors. Slow promotions even under Black supervisors argue against taste-based animus. Instead, the patterns fit models of belief-based discrimination. (JEL J15, J41, J71, M12, M51, O34)

5b51167fb0:4457dc712975ec95.title: Screening and Segmenting: A Consumer Surplus Perspective
5b51167fb0:4457dc712975ec95.author: info@aeaweb.org (Dirk Bergemann1, Tibor Heumann2 and Michael C. Wang3 1 Department of Economics, Yale University (email: dirk.bergemann@yale.edu) 2 Instituto de Economía, Pontificia Universidad…
5b51167fb0:4457dc712975ec95.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3768-3801 Abstract We analyze consumer surplus when a monopolist can adjust both prices and product qualities across segments, engaging in secondand third-degree price discrimination simultaneously. We characterize the consumer-optimal segmentation and show that it has a striking structure: Consumers with the same value receive the same quality in every segment, though prices differ. Under mild conditions, any segmentation harms consumers if and only if demand is sufficiently more elastic than supply. Hence, potential benefits for consumers depend critically on demand and supply elasticities. These findings have implications for regulatory policy regarding price discrimination and market segmentation. (JEL D42, D83, K21, L12, L15)

5b51167fb0:a0b06843547e36d5.title: A Model of the Attention Economy: Data, Platforms, and Discovery
5b51167fb0:a0b06843547e36d5.author: info@aeaweb.org (Daniel Chen1 1 Assistant Professor of Economics, Princeton University (email: dtchen@princeton.edu))
5b51167fb0:a0b06843547e36d5.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3802-3836 Abstract This paper develops a dynamic model of the attention economy featuring two interlinked markets: a product market, where consumers have limited awareness of firms, and an attention market, where platforms attract attention by investing in free services (e.g., social media, streaming, podcasts) and sell targeted ads using data on consumer preferences. The model provides a tractable framework in which platform investment, ad-driven discovery, product demand, and ad revenue are jointly determined. The effects of data and interoperability policies can reverse over time, platform quality may be inefficiently high or low, and the rise of data-rich digital advertising can coincide with a declining ad revenue-to-GDP ratio. (JEL D43, D44, D58, D83, L86, M37)

5b51167fb0:17af0ecaa5dc28ef.title: Fighting for Growth: Labor Scarcity and Technological Progress during the British Industrial Revolution
5b51167fb0:17af0ecaa5dc28ef.author: info@aeaweb.org (Hans-Joachim Voth1, Bruno Caprettini2 and Alex Trew3 1 University of Zurich and CEPR (voth@econ.uzh.ch) 2 University of St. Gallen and CEPR (bruno.caprettini@gmail.com) 3 University…
5b51167fb0:17af0ecaa5dc28ef.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3837-3874 Abstract We establish a link between labor scarcity and the adoption of laborsaving technology in industrializing England. During the Napoleonic Wars, more than 10 percent of the male population served in the armed forces. Where recruitment was heavy, more machines economizing on labor were adopted. Naval recruitment, instrumented by warships' coastal access, provides exogenous variation in labor scarcity and suggests that the link between labor shortages and adoption is causal. Where mechanical skills were abundant, the impact of labor scarcity on adoption appears to be larger. (JEL J24, N13, N43, N63, N73, O14, O31)

5b51167fb0:5713354141b0f2d8.title: Social Push and the Direction of Innovation
5b51167fb0:5713354141b0f2d8.author: info@aeaweb.org (Elias Einiö1, Josh Feng2 and Xavier Jaravel3 1 VATT Institute for Economic Research (email: elias.einio@vatt.fi) 2 University of Utah (email: josh.feng@eccles.utah.edu) 3 London…
5b51167fb0:5713354141b0f2d8.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3875-3909 Abstract What are the implications of unequal access to innovation careers for the direction of innovation and inequality? Leveraging novel linked datasets in the United States and Finland, we document that innovators create products more likely to be purchased by consumers like them in terms of gender, socioeconomic status, and age. Homophily exists both within narrow product categories and across industries and has been stable in recent decades. Incorporating this “social push” channel into a growth model, we estimate that unequal access to innovation careers has a large effect on cost of living inequality and long-run growth. (JEL D63, J16, L26, M13, O31, O33, O47)

5b51167fb0:66d365a090201a2f.title: Knowledge Spillovers, Competition, and Individual Careers
5b51167fb0:66d365a090201a2f.author: info@aeaweb.org (Thomas Cornelissen1, Christian Dustmann2 and Uta Schönberg3 1 Department of Economics, University of Essex, RF Berlin, and Institute for Employment Research (IAB) (email:…
5b51167fb0:66d365a090201a2f.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3910-3941 Abstract Exposure to better peers in the workplace can influence career trajectories through two opposing channels: positively, via knowledge spillovers, and negatively, through competition for advancement. We disentangle these effects by studying untrained labor market entrants and distinguishing between coworkers in the same occupation with whom they are likely to compete versus those with whom they are unlikely to compete. We find robust evidence of persistent knowledge spillovers but also identify countervailing competition effects of comparable magnitude. Both effects are more pronounced for men than for women. (JEL D83, J16, J24, M53, M54, O33)

5b51167fb0:7cf1ce28f4d619bc.title: Truth Elicitation in a Nonstrategic Environment
5b51167fb0:7cf1ce28f4d619bc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Jacob Glazer1 and Ariel Rubinstein2 1 University of Warwick and Tel Aviv University (email: glazer@tauex.tau.ac.il) 2 Tel Aviv University and New York University (email:…
5b51167fb0:7cf1ce28f4d619bc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3942-3958 Abstract A principal decides which party deserves a prize. Only the parties observe the state that determines who is deserving. The principal gives each party a text describing the conditions under which that party deserves the prize and asks each to report the state. The parties are nonstrategic. Each activates a known cheating procedure whose outcome depends on the state and on the text. Implementation is achieved if, whenever the parties disagree, the liar is identified by the “one-way cheating principle”: The truthful party is the unique party who could not have produced his story had the rival's story been true. (JEL D82, D91)

21113a7a19:4a1e5a37dfce9f4e.summary: Silvia Console Battilana, who co-founded Auctionomics along with Paul Milgrom, writes in Forbes about the prospects for market design efforts to help conserve Utah's Great Salt Lake. How Market Design Could Help Save Utah’s Great Salt Lake by By Silvia Console Battilana "the Great Salt Lake is drying up. "To save the lake while protecting water users, business leaders can adopt a little-known but powerful economic tool: market design. When water levels drop, the consequences immediately hit commercial supply chains and local commerce. Market-based incentives give businesses a way to reward upstream water conservation, bringing more water to the lake without hurting regional growth. The invisible hand of the market could identify the least expensive conservation, compensate participating water users and restore the Great Salt Lake. ... "The shrinking of the Great Salt Lake has many causes, and there is no silver-bullet fix. But any solution to refill the lake will likely involve conservation within Utah. Seventy-one percent of the water diverted from the lake’s basin is allocated to agriculture. If those commercial users could make more efficient use of water, more would reach the lake. The catch is that many conservation practices, like water-friendly infrastructure and precision irrigation, are expensive. Under Utah’s traditional “use-it-or-lose-it” water rights system, users have little financial reason to conserve. Without modern economic incentives, asking businesses and farms to voluntarily cut back simply isn’t realistic. Even if water users could be forced to cut back, it’s not clear who should cut back, or by how much. The costs of water conservation aren’t the same across users, and they can be very hard to estimate. Market design can address both of these challenges. Crucially, markets don’t force particular actions or behaviors. Instead, well-designed markets create an incentive for farms and communities to cut back on water and be rewarded for their…

Poetic justice: A review of moral economics by Alvin E. Roth Michael A. Rees "Alvin E. Roth describes poetic justice as the Virginia state flag flying at half-mast in 2020 in honor of Bernie Cohen, who argued the US Supreme Court case Loving v. Virginia that made interracial marriage legal. Turns out Mildred and Richard Loving were convicted of interracial marriage in 1967, arrested by police at 2 AM at home in their bed, and sentenced to 1 year in prison but suspended on the condition that they leave Virginia for 25 years. "Those of us in the field of transplantation have felt—and will continue to feel—the impact of repugnance. In moral economics, Alvin E. Roth takes us on a grand tour of how repugnance shapes transactions across a wide spectrum of human activities. We report a recent single-center experience. Methods KPD exchanges were coordinated within an institutional registry under national supervision. We retrospectively reviewed six consecutive, simultaneous two-way exchanges (12 recipients) from 2022 to 2025. We assessed predefined desensitization failure or anticipated failure with the intended donor, compared immunologic compatibility between intended and exchange donors, and recorded perioperative desensitization, graft function, delayed graft function (DGF), and biopsy-proven acute rejection (BPAR). 21113a7a19:a7d807e7d8608906.title: The once and future market for prostitution in Rhode Island
21113a7a19:a7d807e7d8608906.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:a7d807e7d8608906.summary: Kim Krawiec , the great legal scholar of repugnant transactions, has written that rare (almost never seen) book review that extends the empirical study of an important, well-studied social science event, namely Rhode Island's experience of legal prostitution. It provides an illuminating followup to the germinal paper by Cunningham and Shah. (Prostitution in R.I. is one of the controversial markets covered in Moral Economics , and I believe Krawiec's book review is headed for a forthcoming symposium on the book in Œconomia ­­.) The Smallest State's Big Experiment by Kimberly D. Krawiec October 09, 2026 Abstract Rhode Island’s accidental decriminalization of prostitution in 1980 is typically told as the story of a legal change that went unnoticed for more than two decades. This review of Alvin Roth’s latest book, Moral Economics, challenges that standard account and explores its implications for Roth’s argument that markets need social support to flourish. Drawing on court records, contemporaneous news reports, arrest statistics, and legislative proceedings, I show that the statutory change was noticed almost immediately. Prostitution-related arrests continued, not because police and prosecutors were ignorantly arresting and charging sex workers and clients under a statute that no longer existed, but because the legal system adapted using tools – primarily the loitering prohibition that survived the 1980 rewrite – that have long been used to police behavior and individuals considered repugnant. After a 2003 judicial ruling closed an important enforcement avenue against indoor sex work and vaulted the market into the open, a coalition formed around trafficking concerns that eventually paved the way for recriminalization in 2009. Rhode Island’s accidental experiment with decriminalized sex work provided neither the deliberately designed regulatory framework nor the political backing that could build the type of social support that Roth insists (correctly, in my view)…

The first 100 cases of organ donation after euthanasia in the Netherlands: lessons from preliminary experiences. BMC Med Ethics (2026). https://doi.org/10.1186/s12910-026-01590-5 "Background Organ donation after euthanasia (ODE) is an evolving, patient-initiated procedure in the Netherlands. While it gives meaning to donors at the end-of-life, it introduces complex ethical and practical challenges for healthcare professionals. This study aims to describe the clinical characteristics and donation outcomes of the first 100 ODE procedures in the Netherlands, while outlining the practical and ethical dilemmas encountered. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on prospectively collected data from the first 100 ODE procedures conducted between September 2012 and February 2023. To gain deeper insight into practical experiences and ethical themes, these data were discussed with organ donation coordinators and intensivists involved in the procedures. The analysis focused on clinical characteristics and donation outcomes, as on ethical and practical challenges. Results Neurodegenerative disorders were the primary underlying cause of suffering (52%), followed by psychiatric conditions (31%). The first 100 procedures resulted in 408 transplanted organs. Most procedures were performed in intensive care units, with general practitioners performing euthanasia. Key ethical and practical challenges included the tension between clinical protocols (e.g., fasting) and patient comfort, the medicalisation of the dying process through invasive monitoring, and the logistical barriers of starting ODE from home (ODEH). Faisal, Ahmad, Abdul Khakim Mahfud Zubaidi, Ahmad Nizar Zuhdi Al Hakimi, and Roya Goldoust. “ The Iranian government’s efforts to facilitate foundation-led kidney donation align with the Maqāsid al-Sharī’ah .” Al-Madina: Journal of Islamic Law 1, no. 1 (2026): 28–48. Abstract The issue of kidney transplantation, particularly through compensated living-unrelated donors, represents a complex intersection of medical necessity, ethical debate, and international governance. Iran is unique in legally regulating compensated kidney donation, aiming to address the chronic shortage of transplantable organs while providing structured financial incentives to donors. This study analyzes Iran’s kidney donation system through the lens of maqāsid al-sharī’ah, emphasizing the objective of hifz al-nafs (preservation of life), to evaluate both the ethical legitimacy and life-saving effectiveness of the policy. Employing a qualitative-descriptive approach, the research synthesizes empirical evidence on donor demographics, motivations, compensation mechanisms, and clinical outcomes, alongside normative Islamic ethical considerations and international standards such as the WHO Guiding Principles and the Declaration of Istanbul. Findings reveal that while Iran’s system significantly enhances patient survival and fulfills the core goal of hifz al-nafs, donor participation is heavily influenced by economic necessity, raising ethical concerns about voluntariness, long-term welfare, and equitable access. Moreover, the system’s interaction with foreign patients highlights challenges in cross-border governance and the potential for transplant tourism. The study contributes…

2f5fdda6a0:07a1b8850d9ac432.title: Careers in Finance
2f5fdda6a0:07a1b8850d9ac432.author: Scognamiglio, Annalisa
2f5fdda6a0:07a1b8850d9ac432.summary: Past research has documented a substantial finance wage premium. We examine whether this premium reflects differences in lifetime career opportunities. Using resume data, we reconstruct career trajectories in finance and nonfinance sectors and build synthetic measures of career attractiveness that account for compensation levels, growth, and risk. We find that asset management and investment banking provide a sizable risk-adjusted career premium relative to banking, insurance, and other sectors. This premium has declined across cohorts, particularly relative to high tech. Labor-market entry patterns respond to these premia: potential entrants treat finance and high-tech careers as substitutes when choosing where to start.

2f5fdda6a0:638ae45ef0c67b5e.title: Political Affiliation and Media Distrust: Evidence from Stock Market Investors
2f5fdda6a0:638ae45ef0c67b5e.author: Massa, Massimo
2f5fdda6a0:638ae45ef0c67b5e.summary: Does distrust in politically affiliated media induce a bias in investor beliefs? We study the acquisition of Dow Jones & Co. by News Corporation in 2007 as a shock to the political affiliation of Dow Jones outlets. Following the acquisition, the prices of Republican- (Democrat-) aligned stocks become less sensitive to favorable (unfavorable) Dow Jones Newswires (DJNW) sentiment, consistent with the market attaching less credibility to a politically affiliated source. There is, however, no evidence of change in DJNW sentiment, coverage, or language about Republican/Democrat stocks, suggesting a loss of stock price informativeness. Consistent with this view, a portfolio exploiting the attenuated reaction to DJNW news earns abnormal returns following 2007.

2f5fdda6a0:a7908c944a06eff7.title: Optimal Retirement Saving and Dissaving
2f5fdda6a0:a7908c944a06eff7.author: Munk, Claus
2f5fdda6a0:a7908c944a06eff7.summary: Applying a rich model of individuals’ life-cycle utility maximization, I comprehensively evaluate retirement saving plans. Across a range of individual characteristics, access to basic plans with constant expected payouts and no or full annuitization leads to individual utility gains of up to 5.07% of initial wealth and lifetime income ($43,800 in present value terms), and almost all individuals prefer full annuitization and a target-date fund investment strategy. With flexible plans allowing for partial annuitization and non-constant expected payouts, utility gains go up to 5.81%, and most individuals prefer a high degree of annuitization and expected payouts being increasing through retirement.

2f5fdda6a0:11279647bd188980.title: Household Finance at the Origin: Home Ownership as a Cultural Heritage from Agriculture
2f5fdda6a0:11279647bd188980.author: Vuillemey, Guillaume
2f5fdda6a0:11279647bd188980.summary: I show that home ownership decisions across countries and individuals are shaped by a cultural heritage from agriculture. For centuries, dominant assets in preindustrial economies were either land or cattle. Consequently, the type of farming prevailing locally shaped preferences and beliefs about the relative value of immovable and movable assets. This cultural heritage had long-lasting consequences. Today, individuals originating from societies with a history of crop agriculture—where the dominant asset was land—are more likely to be homeowners. For identification, I rely both on home ownership decisions of second-generation immigrants in the United States and on an instrument.
