b0a91b96f4:13fb9371d133797f.title: Interest Rates and Stock Prices: An Old Debate Flares up!
b0a91b96f4:13fb9371d133797f.author: Aswath Damodaran (noreply@blogger.com)
b0a91b96f4:13fb9371d133797f.summary: The war in Iran, oil prices and worries about a recession have all taken turns driving stock prices in 2026 but talk about interest rates and where they are going has been a constant concern all year. In the last few weeks, interest rate worries have come to the surface again, for three reasons, all related. The first is the rise in long-term US treasury rates to levels not seen in twenty years. The second is US debt exceeding $40 trillion for the first time , bringing attention to a long-standing worry that this debt burden may be hitting a tipping point for bond buyers. The third is a that the Federal Reserve has a new chair in Kevin Warsh, and for the many Fed Watchers, who are uncertain about where he plans to lead the Fed, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting coming up in mid-September looms larger than ever. In this post, I hope to step back from the day-to-day coverage of US treasury yields and look at their performance in 2026, not only with a longer term perspective, but also in the context of movements in long terms yields in government bonds in other currencies. I also intend to revisit a discussion that I initiated in 2022, when interest rates were the central act in markets, about the relationship between interest rates and stock prices, and why higher rates do not always translate into lower stock prices, and why that effect will vary across sectors and companies. Government Borrowing Rates Governments borrow money and often do so by issuing bonds in financial markets. The rates on these bonds reflect the concerns that lenders have about the purchasing power of the currencies that they are issued in, and government bond rates, for better or worse, become indicators that drive day-to-day market movements in almost all asset classes. In this section, I will begin with an examination of US treasury rates before expanding the discussion to government bond rates in other currencies. b0a91b96f4:705ca8baf30517c9.title: The Scaling and Profitability Trade off: Venture Capital's Weakest Link!
b0a91b96f4:705ca8baf30517c9.author: Aswath Damodaran (noreply@blogger.com)
b0a91b96f4:705ca8baf30517c9.summary: It is undeniable technology companies have found their most hospitable setting in the United States and while there are many reasons for the US dominance of technology, easier access to capital for young businesses has been a key ingredient. Venture capital in the US, in its institutional and organized form, can trace its roots back to the 1950s, and over the last few decades, it has generated its share of legendary investors. Vinod Khosla is one of those legends, and it is for that reason that I was surprised to see him tweet the following: I understand that utterances on social media, often in response to comments by others or made in anger, are often quickly regretted, and I believe (though I am not certain) that Mr. Khosla did not quite mean what he said here, confusing profitability with cash flows, and arguing that every business should put scaling ahead of profitability. That said, his view that scaling should be given priority over profitability is more the norm, than the exception, among many venture capitalists, and while it probably always has been the case, I believe the tilt towards scaling has become pronounced in the last two decades. In this post, I want to zero in on the scaling and profitability trade off, how the emphasis on the former over the latter plays out at start-ups and very young companies, and why we live with the consequences, whether they want to or not. Scaling versus Business Building To put the choices you will face on scaling up versus business building into perspective, let's assume that you are a founder, and that your start-up has a tested product and that you believe there is a market for that product. You can stay with what you have built and build a business to take advantage of the immediate market, focusing on financial health and profitability. The fact that you will stay small, and perhaps unrecognized in markets other than your own, is a minus, but there are pluses. You will have little need for external capital, and…

1aa97d921e:bd2718ce7fe44e03.title: Anti-Monopoly as Industrial Policy: The Chicago School Versus Adam Smith
1aa97d921e:bd2718ce7fe44e03.author: Richard R. John
1aa97d921e:bd2718ce7fe44e03.summary: Jolted by the Great Depression of the 1930s, Thurman Arnold devised an anti-monopoly industrial policy for the United States Justice Department that breathed fresh life into a then-moribund Sherman Anti-Trust Act. Arnold’s jurisprudence built on Adam Smith’s discovery that market-making could promote national security and forestall civil unrest. Smith’s insights had informed the industrial policy of Alexander Hamilton, who laid the groundwork in the 1790s for the country’s economic development. Edward H. Levi brought Arnold’s pragmatic anti-monopolism to the University of Chicago. Here, ironically, Arnoldian jurisprudence would be transmogrified into the doctrinaire company-over-country market fundamentalism of the Chicago School of Economics. Today, writes Richard R. John, as we envision for the 21st century a new pro-market, pro-freedom, pro-national security industrial policy, it is worth recalling how U. S. economic development took the form that it did, why the Chicago School repudiated the enduring wisdom of Adam Smith, and what this portends for the world of today. Read it at ProMarket >>

1aa97d921e:93e02838a27ed28b.summary: Adam Smith’s theory of political economy did not begin with the isolated individual but rather the individual who operates to earn the respect of others. In the 1970s and ‘80s, the Chicago School abandoned this aspect of freedom in preference of the isolated individual, which in turn produced a weaker concept of freedom, morality, and society that has stifled the cultivation of all three in the United States, writes Maha Rafi Atal. 59ec699e9f:af16af4a109df3c0.title: Lacunes en matière de compétences des travailleurs selon la perception des employeurs
59ec699e9f:af16af4a109df3c0.author: Genevieve Dufour
59ec699e9f:af16af4a109df3c0.summary: This report uses data from Statistics Canada’s Survey of Employers on Workers’ Skills (SEWS) to provide an overview of the skills sought, available, and developed within Canadian businesses. It focuses in particular on basic mathematics skills, numeracy, critical thinking, and problem-solving, comparing Quebec with Ontario and the rest of Canada. Our results show that basic mathematics skills are rarely perceived as a skills gap by businesses, both in Quebec and elsewhere in Canada. Quebec businesses, however, place relatively greater emphasis on technical, managerial, and computer skills, and less emphasis on critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication, both when recruiting and when developing employees’ skills. The results also show that Quebec businesses differ in how they manage skills. They assess their skills needs less frequently, make less use of informal skills-development practices such as mentoring and feedback, and report greater recruitment difficulties, regardless of the level of education required. Across all three regions, more than half of businesses attribute these difficulties to a lack of interested applicants, suggesting that job attractiveness is as much an issue as an actual shortage of skills. Finally, when faced with skills gaps, businesses tend to favour internal work reorganization rather than investing in human capital development. Ce rapport utilise les données de l’Enquête auprès des employeurs sur les compétences du personnel (EECP) de Statistique Canada pour brosser un portrait des compétences recherchées, disponibles et développées dans les entreprises canadiennes. Il porte une attention particulière aux compétences mathématiques de base, aux capacités de calcul, à la pensée critique et à la résolution de problèmes, en comparant le Québec à l’Ontario et au reste du Canada. Nos résultats montrent que les compétences mathématiques de base sont rarement perçues comme une lacune par les entreprises, au Québec comme ailleurs…

59ec699e9f:ca215887f7b38530.title: Beyond Employment: Minimum Wage Effects on Hours Worked
59ec699e9f:ca215887f7b38530.author: Hikaru Ota
59ec699e9f:ca215887f7b38530.summary: This study estimates the effect of minimum wage increases on low-wage employment and working hours using an event study analysis based on 138 state-level minimum wage changes in the United States. The results show that employment declines in wage bins below the new minimum wage are largely offset by increases in employment at and above it, yielding a near-zero net employment effect. Applying the same wage bin framework to total usual weekly working hours, the analysis finds no significant reduction in total working hours. However, hours worked per worker decrease significantly in the wage bin at the new minimum wage. This pattern may reflect firms adjusting along the intensive margin, but it may also arise from changes in the composition of workers within that wage bin; the analysis cannot distinguish between these explanations. Nevertheless, the findings demonstrate that stable employment levels can mask underlying changes in hours worked.

59ec699e9f:4566d866866f19f5.title: What Aggregation Hides: Disaggregated Wage Returns to Tertiary Education in New Zealand, 2016-2024

59ec699e9f:c6e8101a1e5a5e7c.title: Minimum Wages and Cost-Push Inflation: Economy-Wide Evidence from Germany
59ec699e9f:c6e8101a1e5a5e7c.author: Maximilian Priem
59ec699e9f:c6e8101a1e5a5e7c.summary: We provide the first estimates of minimum wage effects on the aggregate price level using data on the near-full German consumer basket across four national reforms, 2015-2024. Drawing on a structural model of pricing under imperfect competition, we utilise minimum wage cost shocks rather than the commonly used firm-level ‘bite’ that we show to be biased under strategic complementarity. Labour cost pass-through is 83-94 percent, at the higher end of estimates for other cost shocks. The implied macro-price elasticity is 0.024. The largest increase in October 2022 to €12 raised the aggregate price level by 0.39 percent.

59ec699e9f:2be2a6c1df388255.title: Entry Motivations Shape Preferences for Social Protection Among Platform Workers
59ec699e9f:2be2a6c1df388255.author: Thil, Laurène
59ec699e9f:2be2a6c1df388255.summary: We study platform workers' preferences for social protection â€” in the form of sick pay and paid annual leave â€” distinguishing between workers who entered platform work out of economic necessity (the "pushed") and those attracted by its flexibility and advantages (the "pulled"). Using a discrete-choice experiment administered to nearly 800 taxi, delivery, and cleaning platform workers in Germany, Italy, and Poland, we find an average willingness to pay at 3.7% of earnings for sick pay coverage and 4.6% for paid annual leave. Preferences, however, differ sharply by motivation: pushed workers are willing to forgo on average 5.3% of earnings for sick pay, and 5.6% for paid annual leave, while pulled workers' valuations are substantially lower (3.1% and 4.2%, respectively). This difference is most pronounced among workers without access to these benefits, suggesting that the absence of protections is particularly consequential for those who entered platform work under greater economic constraint. The findings indicate that the welfare impact of extending social protections to platform workers â€” as proposed by the EU Platform Work Directive â€” might depend on the share of necessity-driven workers in the platform workforce.

59ec699e9f:0d2acd1a2ef7962d.title: Consumption, Savings, and Earnings Responses to Financial Windfalls
59ec699e9f:0d2acd1a2ef7962d.author: Barry Scholnick
59ec699e9f:0d2acd1a2ef7962d.summary: We estimate the causal effects of a financial windfall on consumption, savings, and wage earnings using linked administrative data on a large sample of Canadian lottery winners. Using separate linkages of lottery winners to income tax records and credit bureau data, we estimate how lottery winnings affect consumption measured through credit card spending, savings through financial asset accumulation and debt repayment, and wage earnings from tax records. We then examine how these responses vary across the income distribution. We find that high-income individuals allocated a larger share of lottery winnings to savings and leisure, while low-income individuals spent a larger share on consumption. We illustrate the policy relevance of these heterogeneous responses through three applications: designing fiscal stimulus programs, evaluating a Universal Basic Income (UBI), and determining optimal top tax rates on wage earnings and savings.

59ec699e9f:96eceb11d490f61c.title: Adolescent Skills, Mental Health, and Early-Adult Educational and Labour-Market Outcomes
59ec699e9f:96eceb11d490f61c.author: Lindsey Macmillan
59ec699e9f:96eceb11d490f61c.summary: We examine how different dimensions of adolescent development---cognitive skills, socio-emotional functioning, and mental health---are associated with educational attainment and labour-market engagement at age 23. Using the Millennium Cohort Study, we show that these dimensions are linked to distinct outcomes in early adulthood. Attention difficulties are most strongly associated with lower educational attainment, while emotional, conduct, and peer difficulties are more closely related to weaker labour-market engagement and a higher likelihood of being not in education, employment, or training (NEET). Persistent behavioural and mental-health difficulties are particularly predictive of NEET status. We further document substantial socioeconomic inequalities in educational attainment and labour-market engagement and assess the extent to which adolescent skills and mental health account for these disparities. Our findings show that different dimensions of adolescent development are associated with distinct pathways through education and into the labour market, while also contributing to persistent socioeconomic inequalities in early-adult outcomes.

59ec699e9f:374c56dc655d6f15.title: Instrumental-Variable Estimation of Fixed-Effects Fractional-Outcome Panel Data Models, with an Application to a Major Disability Support Policy Reform
59ec699e9f:374c56dc655d6f15.author: Staub, Kevin
59ec699e9f:374c56dc655d6f15.summary: We develop a fixed-effects estimation framework for fractional-outcome panel models with a logit conditional mean. Pairwise quasi-differencing eliminates individual effects from the moment conditions, yielding a generalized method of moments estimator that is consistent under the stated moment restrictions even when the number of time period is finite and fixed. The framework allows unrestricted dependence between individual effects and covariates, accommodates endogenous regressors through instrumental variables, and extends to multivariate shares that sum to one. Boundary observations require no adjustment, and average semi-elasticities can be estimated without recovering the individual effects. We apply the framework to Australia's National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), using HILDA (Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia) survey data for 2011-2023 and instruments based on the scheme's staggered geographic rollout. We examine how NDIS receipt affects the allocation of time across paid work, housework, disability care, and remaining activities for recipients and other household members. The estimates indicate that recipients reduce work and disability care, while other household members increase disability care.

59ec699e9f:a77799a51ab463ef.title: The Introduction of Universal Child Care in New Mexico: Initial Evidence on Mothers' Labor Supply
59ec699e9f:a77799a51ab463ef.author: Herbst, Chris
59ec699e9f:a77799a51ab463ef.summary: In November 2025, New Mexico became the first U.S. state to implement a universal, no-cost child care subsidy program. This paper estimates difference-in-differences and event-study models to evaluate the impact of universal child care on mothers' short-run labor supply adjustments. Using monthly Current Population Survey data, I find that the reform produced different responses across lower- and higher-skilled mothers. For lower-skilled mothers, the policy increased employment along both the extensive and intensive margins. Conversely, higher-skilled mothers, particularly those who are married, experienced reductions in paid work, with partially offsetting increases in school enrollment. Thus, while universal child care relaxes a binding constraint among disadvantaged families, it acts as an in-kind transfer for their advantaged counterparts.

59ec699e9f:b09a42580ba445b8.title: Capital-Skill Complementarity Beyond Firm Boundaries
59ec699e9f:b09a42580ba445b8.author: Stijn Vanormelingen
59ec699e9f:b09a42580ba445b8.summary: New machinery has long been argued to raise the relative demand for skilled labor, yet firm-level evidence finds no such shift at investing firms. We resolve this puzzle by looking beyond firm boundaries. Linking Belgian data on capital investments, buyer–supplier transactions, and worker skills, we show that the skill bias of new machinery arises entirely at external suppliers. Following machinery investment spikes, purchases from suppliers raise firms’ total demand for high-STEM workers by 45%, three times the rise for other skill groups, while in-house hiring raises it by less than 5%, evenly across skill groups. This external demand comes first from machine integrators and later from complementary services such as software, and is stronger for smaller firms, lumpier investments, and rapidly advancing capital, consistent with fixed and adjustment costs of hiring high-STEM workers in-house. In a general-equilibrium model estimated on our event studies, the rise in machinery per worker from 2003 to 2021 raises relative demand for high-STEM workers by 8.8 log points and their wage premium by 3.1. Measured on payrolls alone, both would fall.

59ec699e9f:d4c2ef32d1497188.title: Labor Supply and Wages over the Life Cycle: Human Capital and Disability Benefits
59ec699e9f:d4c2ef32d1497188.author: Tom Waters
59ec699e9f:d4c2ef32d1497188.summary: Work experience has been found to be a key determinant of work and wages for educated women, but it seems to play a smaller role for the less educated. For them, welfare, tax credits and family composition matter more, and increasingly so does participation in disability programmes. Here we document how labor supply, wages, health, and disability claims have evolved in the UK over the last three decades, and examine how reforms to tax credits, disability benefits and other welfare programs have changed work incentives over this period. We then introduce these features into an empirical dynamic structural model of life-cycle labor supply, human capital and disability benefit application, in which human capital combines health capital, experience accumulated in work, and education. Estimating the model on a panel of working-age women in the UK, we examine the interactions between experience capital and health capital in driving life-cycle earnings across different education groups. Our results highlight the importance of interactions in the disability benefit, welfare and tax-credit systems for understanding the life cycle pattern of hours, employment, earnings, and disability claims, and for evaluating policy counterfactuals.

59ec699e9f:dec6e54e4738e321.title: Physicians' Occupational Licensing and the Quantity-Quality Trade-off
59ec699e9f:dec6e54e4738e321.author: Cristóbal Otero
59ec699e9f:dec6e54e4738e321.summary: Occupational licensing is a widespread quality regulation that potentially increases the quality of labor but reduces its quantity. We provide a theoretical framework to empirically quantify this trade-off in public hospitals, where both clinical quality and physician shortages are critical concerns. Using quasi-exogenous variation driven by a recent and unprecedented migration of physicians to Chile, together with growth in domestic medical schools, we show that more physicians improve patient outcomes, while lower-quality physicians—as measured by licensing exam performance—worsen them. Incorporating these findings into our theoretical framework, we evaluate the implications of locally changing the stringency of the licensing policy.

59ec699e9f:e18367ee31a0e58b.title: How Heavily Are PhD Students Offloading Their Scientific Writing to AI? Evidence from US STEM PhD Dissertations
59ec699e9f:e18367ee31a0e58b.author: Hansen Zhang
59ec699e9f:e18367ee31a0e58b.summary: Large language models are diffusing rapidly into science, raising concerns that delegating research writing to AI may undermine the development of expertise that scientific training is supposed to build. We measure AI-generated writing in the dissertations of a near-census of US STEM PhD graduates from 2019 to 2026 and link graduates to their subsequent employment. AI writing is absent before 2023, present in 29% of dissertations filed in 2026, and rapidly growing. Use is more common among students from non-English-speaking countries and at lower-ranked programs. Among graduates in the same program and cohort, those whose dissertations contain AI writing are less likely to enter academic research careers and more likely to enter non-tenure-track roles or industry, with this pattern strongest among US-origin students. At the same time as AI may increase research productivity, it thus appears to also be displacing a potentially important portion of the work through which scientific expertise is developed.

59ec699e9f:c5b030775cec6849.title: Consumption, Savings, and Earnings Responses to Financial Windfalls
59ec699e9f:c5b030775cec6849.author: Barry Scholnick
59ec699e9f:c5b030775cec6849.summary: We estimate the causal effects of a financial windfall on consumption, savings, and wage earnings using linked administrative data on a large sample of Canadian lottery winners. Using separate linkages of lottery winners to income tax records and credit bureau data, we estimate how lottery winnings affect consumption measured through credit card spending, savings through financial asset accumulation and debt repayment, and wage earnings from tax records. We then examine how these responses vary across the income distribution. We find that high-income individuals allocated a larger share of lottery winnings to savings and leisure, while low-income individuals spent a larger share on consumption. We illustrate the policy relevance of these heterogeneous responses through three applications: designing fiscal stimulus programs, evaluating a Universal Basic Income (UBI), and determining optimal top tax rates on wage earnings and savings.

59ec699e9f:5e726b4adc7b0fe8.title: Workers, Firms, and Spatial Wage Inequality: Evidence from Hungarian Local Labor Markets
59ec699e9f:5e726b4adc7b0fe8.author: László Czaller
59ec699e9f:5e726b4adc7b0fe8.summary: This paper examines how workers and employers jointly shape spatial wage disparities across Hungarian local labor markets. We combine longitudinal linked employer–employee administrative data for 2012–2022 with functional local labor markets constructed from district-to-district commuting flows in the 2022 Hungarian Census. Our preferred delineation contains 29 commuting zones and raises the share of employed residents working within the same unit above 90 percent, compared with 72 percent for districts and 81 percent for counties. We estimate an additive worker–employer fixed-effect wage model and decompose wage variation at the individual level, between commuting zones, and within commuting zones. Differences in commuting-zone mean wages account for 2.8 percent of national log-wage variance and 1.1 percent when the Budapest commuting zone is excluded. Although the between-zone component is modest, its structure is systematic: zones with higher average worker effects also tend to have higher average employer wage premia, so the spatial alignment of worker and employer components accounts for an important part of spatial wage differences. Wage dispersion and the relative importance of worker heterogeneity, employer premia, and worker–employer sorting within local labor markets also vary substantially across the country. The results indicate that spatial wage disparities in Hungary reflect not only differences in workers’ earnings potential and the employer premia attached to their jobs, but also how these components are combined across local labor markets.

59ec699e9f:a447ce1c46303d0e.title: Which Workers Left the Labor Force Post-COVID Recession and Why?: Filing, Tax Credit Take-Up, and Labor Force Engagement by Occupation
59ec699e9f:a447ce1c46303d0e.author: Michael Stevens
59ec699e9f:a447ce1c46303d0e.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic caused a sharp initial rise in unemployment, followed by an unexpectedly tight labor market. Using a panel of tax data containing newly assembled information on worker occupation, we document persistent labor force exit, especially among low-income and low-skill workers. Low-skilled unmarried men are by far the most likely to exit, reinforcing recent concerns regarding the economic and social engagement of this group. Contrary to prevailing theories, we find little evidence that school closures, virus exposure, stimulus payments, or unemployment benefits explain these exits. Nor is the exit explained by additional upgrading of occupations or firm quality. Individuals who leave the labor force do not (on average) make up the missing income; however, self-employment income replaces roughly a quarter of the lost W-2 income. The facts suggest that the willingness to work for low pay decreased and preferences for leisure and job flexibility increased among a large set of workers who have found ways to get by with less income. These results have implications for tax policy, fiscal projections, and labor market dynamics in the post-pandemic economy.

59ec699e9f:0a01c3a05b0d2cb2.title: Gang Crackdowns
59ec699e9f:0a01c3a05b0d2cb2.author: María Micaela Sviatschi
59ec699e9f:0a01c3a05b0d2cb2.summary: What are the consequences of restoring state authority in territories governed by criminal organizations? Combining household surveys and administrative records with detailed maps of former gang-controlled areas, we study how El Salvador’s 2022 State of Exception, which ended two decades of gang territorial control, reshaped Salvadoran society. We find that the removal of gang control integrated previously segmented labor markets, improving mobility, employment outcomes, household income, and financial inclusion. Areas with greater pre-2022 gang exposure also experienced larger increases in business formation and property investment. However, the legacy of criminal governance persists through residence-based discrimination: employers remain less willing to hire otherwise identical applicants from former gang-controlled neighborhoods. Finally, although overall support for the crackdowns remains high, individuals who witnessed police abuse report substantially greater distrust of the police and the national government, suggesting that abuses of state authority may undermine the political sustainability of tough-on-crime policies.

59ec699e9f:876437d22495089d.title: Avoiding Regulation: Evidence from Nursing Homes
59ec699e9f:876437d22495089d.author: Riley League
59ec699e9f:876437d22495089d.summary: We study strategic responses by firms to threshold-based regulations. We document extensive bunching in response to additional staffing requirements for California nursing homes with at least 100 beds. To estimate the regulation’s effect on staffing, we develop a novel treatment effects estimator for threshold-based regulations under precise manipulation, by decomposing firms into response types based on counterfactual and realized staffing and size, separating causal effects from selection. We estimate that higher staffing above the threshold is nearly entirely due to selection, with low-staffing facilities manipulating their size to avoid the regulation. These size distortions limit access, particularly for disadvantaged patients.

59ec699e9f:36f08e7f123cb64b.title: Schooling and Political Activism in the Early Civil Rights Era
59ec699e9f:36f08e7f123cb64b.author: Bhashkar Mazumder
59ec699e9f:36f08e7f123cb64b.summary: Does education lead to political activity? We find that a large, early 20th century school construction program, the Rosenwald schools, led to more NAACP branches in the rural South starting in the early 1940s, i.e. prior to the classic U.S. Civil Rights Movement. Branch growth was stronger where Jim Crow occupational segregation prevented Black men from realizing some of the economic gains of their education. Our findings lend support to theories emphasizing that economic context can act as a critical mediator in determining whether human capital causes political engagement.

59ec699e9f:f6618a5a531cd251.title: Asymmetric Information in Wage Contracts: Experimental Evidence and Welfare Implications
59ec699e9f:f6618a5a531cd251.author: Daniel Herbst
59ec699e9f:f6618a5a531cd251.summary: Compared to self-employment or performance-based pay, fixed wages reduce earnings uncertainty but are prone to market distortions through moral hazard and adverse selection. Using a model of wage contracts under asymmetric information, I show that these distortions map to marginal treatment response functions in a marginal treatment effects (MTE) framework. I apply this framework to a field experiment in which data-entry workers choose between a randomized fixed wage and a piece rate. I find evidence of both moral hazard and adverse selection: Fixed wages reduce worker productivity by an estimated 8.74 percent relative to the mean. Meanwhile, a 10 percent increase in the wage offer attracts a marginal worker whose productivity is higher by 1.90 percent of the mean. Using semi-parametric MTE estimation, I calculate the welfare loss associated with asymmetric information and the marginal values of public funds (MVPFs) for policies aimed at recovering this loss. I find that a tax on piece rates can mitigate adverse selection into fixed wages, generating tax revenue at social costs as low as $0.88 per dollar.

59ec699e9f:d6a700b3dd4eeed9.title: High and Rising Institutional Concentration of Award-Winning Economists
59ec699e9f:d6a700b3dd4eeed9.author: Hanzhang Zhou
59ec699e9f:d6a700b3dd4eeed9.summary: We analyze the academic affiliations of nearly 6, 000 award-winning researchers in 18 major fields in the natural sciences, engineering, and social sciences from the 1820s to the 2020s, focusing on the 1960s onward. The analysis reveals a trend of declining concentration in the institutional affiliations of award-winning researchers, shifting from a few science-strong universities in high-income countries to a more diverse set of institutions across the world. The decline in concentration is observed in all fields except one: economics. The institutional affiliations of prizewinning economists have become more concentrated over time, making economics the most concentrated field. We associate the higher concentration of prizewinning work in economics with the field’s stronger sorting by institutional prestige, its lower reliance on specialized equipment and instruments, and its assessment of findings based on a synthesis of evidence rather than on decisive experiments or proofs. We discuss the benefits and costs of this high and rising institutional concentration of prizewinning economists.

59ec699e9f:7fb14afce539e12b.title: Digital Social Pressure, Managerial Decision-Making and Worker Performance: Evidence from Professional Football
59ec699e9f:7fb14afce539e12b.author: James Reade
59ec699e9f:7fb14afce539e12b.summary: Digital platforms expose workers and managers to immediate, public, and persistent evaluations from external audiences, creating a form of social pressure that may shape workplace decisions. We examine whether such digital social pressure predicts subsequent opportunity allocation and worker performance, using professional football as a high-frequency empirical setting. We link player-match data from Europeâ€™s five major leagues to post-match Twitter commentary and construct measures of negative sentiment, toxicity, and racial abuse. Comparing players with themselves over time and teammates in the same current match, we find that greater negative sentiment is associated with a lower probability of appearing in the teamâ€™s next match. Toxicity shows a similar but less stable association, while racial-abuse intensity is imprecisely estimated when the measures enter jointly. By contrast, associations with performance conditional on a subsequent appearance are small and imprecise. Overall, the findings suggest that digital social pressure is reflected more strongly in the allocation of subsequent opportunities than in worker performance, showing how public evaluations generated outside formal organizational boundaries can become part of the reputational environment surrounding internal managerial decisions.

59ec699e9f:d7ac4d46dd478bfe.title: Seniority rules and selection into job loss
59ec699e9f:d7ac4d46dd478bfe.author: Häggkvist, Martin
59ec699e9f:d7ac4d46dd478bfe.summary: How much are employers willing to pay to sidestep employment protection? I study this in the context of seniority rules, aiming to shield tenured workers from job loss. Using detailed and unique Swedish layoff notification data matched with administrative registers, I identify the set of workers at risk of dismissal and construct counterfactual displacement lists based on the mandated layoff order. I find that workplaces with relatively more productive junior workers are significantly less likely to follow the seniority order. A one-standard-deviation increase in the relative productivity of recent hires reduces compliance by 7.7 percentage points. To circumvent the default order, employers provide higher severance pay and longer advance notice to senior workers, indicating that firms pay for the right to retain more productive workers. These results indicate that seniority rules impose efficiency costs on employers as employment protection is traded for financial compensation.

59ec699e9f:256b087b76b355e6.title: The Recent Evolution of AI-Related Labor Demand
59ec699e9f:256b087b76b355e6.author: Kevin Rinz
59ec699e9f:256b087b76b355e6.summary: AI mentions in US job advertisements have increased substantially since the beginning of 2024. The increase is concentrated in occupations more intensely exposed to the capabilities of large language models: one additional standard deviation of exposure is associated with a 3.1 percentage point increase in the rate at which job ads mention AI. Alongside this increase in AI mentions, more exposed occupations have seen job postings stabilize after a period of relative decline, posted wages rise, and hires and separations rise, all relative to less exposed occupations. Realized wages for new hires have risen consistent with posted wages, while wages of continuously employed workers have declined, possibly because exposed occupations have seen labor markets become less tight.

59ec699e9f:6304be0cb15558aa.title: Human Capital Accumulation Across Space
59ec699e9f:6304be0cb15558aa.author: Esteban Rossi-Hansberg
59ec699e9f:6304be0cb15558aa.summary: This paper studies how human capital shapes the economic geography of development. We propose a model in which human capital acquisition costs vary across space, and regions with higher human capital invest more in human-capital-augmenting technology. Locations are interconnected through costly migration and trade. Using data on local income and schooling, we quantify the model at a 1° x 1° resolution globally. Over two centuries, the model mostly predicts persistence in the spatial distribution of development. Proportionally lowering education costs in sub-Saharan Africa raises local outcomes but lowers global welfare, while the same policy in Latin America improves global welfare. An alternative policy that equalizes educational costs across sub-Saharan Africa generates worse outcomes, as population shifts within the region toward less productive areas. These results are driven by the estimated negative correlation between education costs and local fundamentals, as well as spatial inefficiencies due to externalities.

59ec699e9f:c589c429fb1ca891.title: Assessing Financial Preparedness in Old Age in Asia: Evidence from the Republic of Korea
59ec699e9f:c589c429fb1ca891.author: Donghyun Park
59ec699e9f:c589c429fb1ca891.summary: We estimate expected financial resources in old age—including public transfers, family transfers, accumulated assets, and post-retirement labor income—and compare them with target consumption needs. The sample is divided into a reference group (individuals at or beyond retirement age) and a target group (pre-retirement individuals). Two retirement scenarios are considered: (i) a statutory retirement age of 62 for both men and women, and (ii) effective retirement ages of 66 for men and 65 for women. Results are presented by gender and place of residence. We find substantial heterogeneity in financial preparedness, with women facing significantly larger shortfalls than men. Continued work and family transfers remain critical pillars of old-age support, highlighting the transitional nature of the Republic of Korea’s welfare regime.

59ec699e9f:001fd3f07fce3e37.title: Applying but not Receiving: Longer Working Lives and Institutionalized Health Investment
59ec699e9f:001fd3f07fce3e37.author: Felix Weinhardt
59ec699e9f:001fd3f07fce3e37.summary: Rising life expectancy and demographic change have increased the share of older workers, making their health and productivity central to aging societies. We study whether longer working lives translate into investments in work-related health before retirement. Exploiting a pension reform in Germany in a Regression Discontinuity Design, we show that women facing longer careers are more likely to apply for work-related rehabilitation, particularly those in poorer health or with weaker labor market attachment. Despite higher application and approval rates, this demand does not translate into higher rehabilitation completion. Together with intermediate outcomes, our findings are most consistent with capacity constraints in program delivery.

59ec699e9f:2c2f4f2e8a78ab2b.title: Educating like China
59ec699e9f:2c2f4f2e8a78ab2b.author: Yuan Zi
59ec699e9f:2c2f4f2e8a78ab2b.summary: This paper shows that human capital accumulation can accelerate structural transformation without accelerating growth. We study China's 1999 higher education expansion, a large, rapid, and largely unanticipated increase in college graduates. We find that more exposed prefectures experienced larger increases in the skilled-labor share and shifted employment and value added from agriculture toward services. The reallocation extended to low-skilled workers. Consumer services absorbed most of the increase in employment, while producer services accounted for a disproportionate share of high-skilled employment growth. Yet more-exposed prefectures did not grow faster. A four-sector model rationalizes these patterns, showing how greater skill supply can generate broad-based servitization, but also a Baumol-type growth penalty when labor reallocates toward slower-growing sectors. Our findings highlight that the payoff to higher education depends not only on how much skill it creates, but also on whether the resulting structural transformation directs resources toward the economy's engines of productivity growth.

59ec699e9f:6ab7732edcb540ec.title: Vacancy referrals and broader job search: the role of spillovers among caseworkers
59ec699e9f:6ab7732edcb540ec.author: Hossain, Mohammad Zariab
59ec699e9f:6ab7732edcb540ec.summary: This paper provides the first causal evidence of behavioral spillovers in public employment services (PES). Using rich Swedish administrative data from 2004–2018 and a difference-in-differences design exploiting caseworker moves across local PES offices, I show that caseworker’s broader vacancy referral behavior—vacancy referrals outside a job seeker’s stated preferences—responds strongly to the local work-practice styles. I also examine how these practice-environment shocks of the movers (caseworkers) affect their job seekers. Taken together, the evidence suggests that local referral practices and the surrounding organizational environment play an important role in shaping caseworker behavior, with consequences for job seekers’ reemployment prospects.

59ec699e9f:4239734b7ce55501.title: Better Technology, Worse Motivation: Generative Artificial Intelligence’s Mediocrity Trap
59ec699e9f:4239734b7ce55501.author: Zibo Zhao
59ec699e9f:4239734b7ce55501.summary: While generative artificial intelligence (AI) promises productive efficiency, it can paradoxically lead to lower quality work. We conducted an experiment with professional illustrators and found that AI assistance flattens the quality curve—it accelerates initial gains but sharply diminishes the returns on sustained effort. Faced with this, a significant number of professionals made a strategic choice: they sacrificed the final quality to save time. Our finding highlights a critical challenge for generative AI, which can weaken the motivation required for creative excellence and innovation. In developing economies, where governments may seek to boost growth by using generative AI to substitute for scarce skills, our results suggest that such gains may come at the cost of the sustained effort through which higher-quality work and expertise are built.

59ec699e9f:8f373fc12a89bb60.title: Assessing the macroeconomic and fiscal effects of non-communicable diseases
59ec699e9f:8f373fc12a89bb60.author: OECD
59ec699e9f:8f373fc12a89bb60.summary: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) impose substantial costs on economies by reducing workforce participation and productivity, increasing healthcare expenditure and affecting public finances. Quantifying these costs helps policymakers assess the potential economic and fiscal gains from public health policies that reduce the burden of NCDs. The OECD has developed a framework [O1.1] that combines its OECD SPHeP NCDs microsimulation model, which projects the effects of NCDs on population health, labour market outcomes and healthcare expenditure, with the OECD long-term growth model. Previously, the framework estimated the burden of NCDs on GDP through their effects on workforce participation and productivity. This paper extends the framework by adding healthcare expenditure as a second channel through which NCDs affect GDP, capturing how resources used to treat NCDs could otherwise support investment and capital accumulation in the economy. It also broadens the analysis to assess how NCDs affect public expenditure, including healthcare, pensions and other age-related spending. Applied to four major NCDs across 49 OECD, EU and G20 countries, the enhanced framework provides a more comprehensive assessment of their burden on GDP and public finances.

59ec699e9f:21b16bac984c5676.title: Distributional Intersectional Fairness in AI-Supported Job Matching: Evidence on Amplification, Trade-Offs, and Residual Risk
59ec699e9f:21b16bac984c5676.author: Weber, Enzo
59ec699e9f:21b16bac984c5676.summary: "Despite widespread recognition of intersectionality in discrimination research, most algorithmic fairness evaluations remain limited to single-attribute group comparisons or individual-level prediction errors. This paper introduces a distributional approach to intersectional fairness that evaluates how machine learning models reshape the allocation of outcomes across intersecting social groups. Using large-scale administrative labour-market data from public employment services, we analyse an AI-supported job matching system with 141 occupational classes and more than three million observations. We measure intersectional disparities via Jensen–Shannon divergence and compare observed occupational distributions to model-implied allocations. We show that unconstrained models do not merely reproduce existing labour-market structures but systematically amplify intersectional disparities across occupations. Fairness-aware regularization reduces aggregate disparities but introduces a pronounced trade-off with predictive performance and reallocates distortions across occupations rather than eliminating them. Counterfactual averaging achieves substantial reductions in occupation-level disparities while preserving most predictive performance, may provide a more favourable fairness-performance trade-off in this application setting than directly constraining model outcomes. To identify localized fairness risks, we propose an occupation-level audit mechanism that flags cases with unusually large distributional shifts. Even under strong fairness constraints, a small number of occupations exhibit substantial residual distortions, indicating that fairness interventions compress rather than remove inequality. Our results demonstrate that fairness in large-scale decision-support systems must be evaluated at the level of outcome distributions. More broadly, they highlight the limits of purely technical mitigation and the need to combine fairness-aware modelling with explainability,…

4a32a2255e:bb760a062e7cf749.title: The Costs of Access: Freeway Disamenities Across U.S. Cities
4a32a2255e:bb760a062e7cf749.author: Jeffrey Lin
4a32a2255e:bb760a062e7cf749.summary: We construct city-level measures of freeway disamenities and examine their association with metropolitan growth. We combine neighborhood-level estimates from Brinkman and Lin (2024) with calibrated spatial models for U.S. metropolitan areas. Each city measure is based on a counterfactual that removes estimated disamenities while holding modeled travel times fixed. Cities with larger estimated disamenities grew more slowly, conditioned on total freeway mileage and initial population. Total freeway mileage is positively associated with growth in the same specification. Estimated disamenities are larger in cities with greater 1950 populations, more centralized freeway networks, and coastal geography. These patterns are consistent with local quality-of-life costs attenuating regional access related growth benefits.

4a32a2255e:0f2aa77e10d8dd28.title: Agglomeration, the Price-Index Effect, and Migration in Post-NAFTA Mexico
4a32a2255e:0f2aa77e10d8dd28.author: Keisuke Kondo
4a32a2255e:0f2aa77e10d8dd28.summary: This study examines how multiple agglomeration and dispersion forces shaped Mexico’s regional economic geography during the early post-NAFTA period. When economic activity becomes geographically concentrated, consumers gain better access to differentiated varieties and face lower effective transport costs, reducing the local consumption price index and making a region more attractive as a migration destination. Building on this price-index mechanism from New Economic Geography, we focus on four spatial forces: proximity to the U.S. market, the manufacturing price-index effect, the service price-index effect, and density-related urban costs. Using bilateral interstate migration between 1995 and 2000, we proceed in two stages. First, we estimate the structural parameters of the model and recover state-level price indices for manufactured goods and services. Second, we examine how destination–origin differences in nominal wages, price indices, and urban costs are associated with migration across sectors, while controlling for the additional locational advantage of U.S. border states. The manufacturing price index is strongly and negatively associated with migration of manufacturing workers, whereas its cross-sector effects are more limited. By contrast, the service price index is negatively and significantly associated with migration across all sectors, indicating a broad domestic agglomeration force. Employment density is generally negatively associated with migration, consistent with urban costs acting as a centrifugal force, while real-wage differentials are positively associated with migration across most industries. Taken together, the findings suggest that post-NAFTA Mexico was shaped by the interaction of border-oriented manufacturing agglomeration, domestic service-sector agglomeration, and urban-cost-driven dispersion.

4a32a2255e:cc6bd3f1bb61011e.title: University as catalyst of public R&D expenditures? An empirical assessment on EU NUTS 3 regions
4a32a2255e:cc6bd3f1bb61011e.author: Saverio Barabuffi
4a32a2255e:cc6bd3f1bb61011e.summary: This study examines whether universities shape the regional innovation effects of public R&D expenditure and whether this role varies across regional development trajectories. We analyse a panel of 1166 EU NUTS 3 regions over the period 2007-2020, combining data on European public R&D funding, patenting performance, university presence and regional development traps. Toa ddress the endogeneity of public R&D expenditure, we employ a control function aproach. The results show that public r&D expendirue positively affects patenting performance in both university and non-university, but the difference between them is not statistically significant. University presence therefore does not sistematically amplify the returns to public R&D. However, its moderating role becomes more pronounced in regions exposed to development trap risk and in regions experiencing persistent stagnation, while evidence is weaker for trap intensity. These fundings suggest that universities act as contingent rather than unviersal catalyst of public R&D. Their contribution appears particularly relevant in vulnerable and persistently stagnant regional trajectories, but less able to offset sever structural constraints. The study contributes to debates on the geography of public R&D and regional development traps by showing that the effectiveness of research funding depends not only on institutional presence, bu also on the development rajectory in which that institutional capacity is embedded.

4a32a2255e:8d0d5b86ce87e39e.title: Regional Dynamics of Innovation in Europe 2000-2020 A Tale of Convergence, Persistence, and the Illusion of Catch-Up
4a32a2255e:8d0d5b86ce87e39e.author: Michael Wyrwich
4a32a2255e:8d0d5b86ce87e39e.summary: This study examines the dynamics of regional innovation activity in Europe from 2000 to 2020 using patent applications. Standard convergence measures indicate that regional disparities are narrowing, with initially lagging regions catching up to the leading ones. Our analysis reveals two persistent â€˜clubsâ€™: the â€˜laggingâ€™ and the â€˜advancedâ€™ regions. Although these groups are becoming increasingly similar, the differences between them remain largely unchanged. Despite two decades of growth, the disparity between the two clubs still accounts for a great deal of the total variation in regional patenting. These patterns suggest a convergence illusion that is overlooked in the current scholarly debate.

4a32a2255e:819db0d28f02456e.title: Self-Employment and Regional Development in Disruptive Times - Germany 1895 - 2020
4a32a2255e:819db0d28f02456e.author: Michael Wyrwich
4a32a2255e:819db0d28f02456e.summary: We examine the long-term relationship between historical levels of self-employment and economic performance in different regions of Germany. A particular distinction is made between West Germany and the eastern part of the country, that came after WWII for forty years under socialist regime. Regional self-employment rates exhibit high correlation over time periods exceeding a century. In West Germany, high and increasing levels of self-employment are significantly associated with high current levels of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per population, despite several major historical shocks. That such a relationship cannot be found in East Germany could be a legacy of the socialist period where the government performed anti-entrepreneurial policies. We also find a positive relationship between historical self-employment and patenting in both parts of the country. This relationship is, however, somewhat weaker in East Germany, which experienced considerably more historical shocks than West Germany.

4a32a2255e:481dec399fcd21c4.title: The Differential Economic Effects of Private Universities in Urban and Rural Regions
4a32a2255e:481dec399fcd21c4.author: Garcia Chavez, Cecilia
4a32a2255e:481dec399fcd21c4.summary: We investigate whether the local economic effects of niche university actors depend on regional context. Focusing on private university campuses in Germany, we exploit their staggered foundation between 1990 and 2020 and estimate their effects using a conditional staggered difference-in-differences design at the postal-code level. Campus foundations raise local economic activity, but only gradually, with effects becoming statistically significant after about ten years. The effects are strongest in rural and intermediate regions, while urban regions show no significant effects. This pattern supports our argument that niche universities have greater potential to become significant actors in institutionally thinner rural regions.

4a32a2255e:77964f65df06a962.title: A 'Justice Doughnut' approach to reconciling directionality and subsidiarity in regional development: Evidence from green transition in North Sweden
4a32a2255e:77964f65df06a962.author: Grillitsch, Markus
4a32a2255e:77964f65df06a962.summary: As green transitions accelerate, the resulting socio-technical transformations often produce uneven spatial impacts, generating 'green' discontent in peripheral and rural regions. Despite the growing discourse on 'just transition', regional policy models frequently overlook the multidimensional nature of justice. Through this study we explore how justice can be conceptualized and operationalized within regional green transitions? Theoretically, we propose a framework – the justice doughnut- that positions the trivalent approach (distributional, procedural, and recognitional justice) in regional development. We situate this framework amidst the evolving tensions between top-down 'directionality' (driven by sustainability mandates and strategic autonomy) and bottom-up 'subsidiarity' (rooted in place-based policy). We hence recontextualise justice as a mutually constitutive space that mediates the governance of regional transformations. Empirically, we illustrate this framework with a case study in Jämtland-Härjedalen, a peripheral region in North Sweden, vital to national transition ambitions. Employing an abductive, multi-method qualitative design - incorporating policy analysis, stakeholder interviews, and deliberative workshops- we examine the multilevel interactions between local, national, and EU actors. The findings reveal pervasive asymmetries in resources and legitimacy, alongside significant intra-regional differentiation. By highlighting how governance logics shape justice outcomes, we offer a generative lens for rethinking just regional development. We, hence, contribute to a deeper understanding of the institutional conditions necessary to reconcile national transition goals with regional equity in peripheral European contexts.

4a32a2255e:2b6a62de4bd64919.title: A Nation of Contrast? The Geography of Personality in Sweden, Regional Polarization, and a Research Agenda
4a32a2255e:2b6a62de4bd64919.author: Gosling, Samuel D.
4a32a2255e:2b6a62de4bd64919.summary: Personality traits (e.g., the Big Five) shape human behavior, decision-making, and life outcomes. Evidence from various countries suggests that these traits are not randomly distributed but follow systematic regional patterns, fueling interest in their geographical variation. Prior research shows that regional personality compositions can influence—and be influenced by—regional socio-economic development. Here, we present an initial personality map of Sweden based on N = 22, 225 geo-coded personality assessments at the municipal level. In contrast to Sweden's reputation for equality, our analysis reveals notable regional contrasts in personality composition. The data show geographical patterns in adaptive traits (Extraversion, Conscientiousness, Emotional Stability [low Neuroticism]), known predictors of better psychological functioning. Sweden's rust belt exhibits notably lower levels of these traits, while the southernmost region (mainly Scania) shows higher levels. These patterns align with ongoing discussions on regional socio-economic polarization in Sweden and may reflect a macro-psychological imprint of these processes. We therefore propose a future research agenda to examine the causes and consequences of these regional personality variations, while considering potential policy implications.

4a32a2255e:115d2da7670538fa.title: Tracing local well-being through time and space: From an operationalization to a research agenda
4a32a2255e:115d2da7670538fa.author: Hall, Ola
4a32a2255e:115d2da7670538fa.summary: This paper develops and applies a multidimensional indicator of objective well-being grounded in the capabilities approach to analyze spatial and temporal patterns across Swedish municipalities from 2002 to 2020. Operationalizing well-being as a place-based capability environment across six dimensions – economic, health, education, safety, civic, and inclusion – the study moves beyond income-centered accounts of regional inequality and examines how different dimensions of well-being are jointly shaped by local institutional and socioeconomic contexts. The analysis reveals that well-being is persistently structured by municipality type and industrial composition, yet in ways that defy a simple urban advantage: large municipalities lead on economic and educational dimensions but score systematically lower on safety and inclusion, while rural and small municipalities display more balanced capability profiles. Over the study period, well-being improved broadly but unevenly, with rural and peripheral municipalities converging toward the national median while former industrial towns experienced broad-based capability decline across multiple dimensions. The geography of well-being has increasingly aligned with the geography of political discontent, with electoral support for the Sweden Democrats growing strongest in capability-disadvantaged municipalities. Together, these findings advance a spatially grounded, multidimensional understanding of territorial inequality and offer a framework for identifying where structural disadvantage and capability deprivation intersect most acutely.

4a32a2255e:7ec915a0852f8244.title: Local Agency on the Edge: Regional Development, Human Wellbeing and Social Resilience
4a32a2255e:7ec915a0852f8244.author: Horvat, Andrej
4a32a2255e:7ec915a0852f8244.summary: Local agency on the edge relates to situations that are particularly harsh and difficult, places where regional development is most needed but also most difficult to achieve. We study the role and relevance of local agency in such situations, as well as enabling and hindering conditions for local agency to emerge. We do this in two peripheral municipalities in Ukraine that were attacked and temporarily occupied by Russian forces but have shown a high degree of resilience. Theoretically, we propose a broad conception of development, which includes human wellbeing and social resilience. Such a broad conception also necessitates a more comprehensive understanding of local agency underpinning development, including social and technological innovation, institutional entrepreneurship and place-based leadership. The cases provide evidence for the potential development impact of bottom-up initiatives, which may unfold if local actors are sufficiently empowered. In the context of the study, a governance reform played an important role comprising decentralisation and municipal amalgamation in the wider context of a mindset change in favour of approximation towards the European Union. Local actors changed institutions, leading to better governance and participation from the citizens. Empowerment of local actors allowed for the successful implementation of multiple projects impacting citizens' wellbeing, improving health and education institutions, as well as cultural, sports and recreation facilities. These changes opened opportunities for increased entrepreneurial activity, contributing towards employment and tax revenue. Moreover, resilience to the Russian invasion rested on improved governance, relationships, citizen engagement, and capacities for project management developed before the war.

4a32a2255e:506eda741f3f7e74.title: Unlocking Firm Innovation in Peripheral Regions: The Critical Role of Local Psychological Openness
4a32a2255e:506eda741f3f7e74.author: Obschonka, Martin
4a32a2255e:506eda741f3f7e74.summary: Firms in peripheral and less knowledge endowed regions often struggle with innovation, as it is deeply rooted in and influenced by local characteristics. Although recent research highlights the significant, yet complex and hard-to-quantify role of local 'soft factors' such as culture and macro-psychology (e.g., local psychological openness) for firm innovation, we know relatively little about its specific role for firms located in the knowledge periphery. This study examines the hypothesis that favorable local soft factors, such as psychological openness, can compensate for unfavorable local hard factors for innovation of firms located in the knowledge periphery. Drawing upon Schmookler's scissor metaphor, we theoretically elaborate how local psychological openness impacts firm innovation by shaping both the demand and supply sides of the innovation process. In our arguments, we also incorporated the contingent impact of both regional (external) and firm (internal) factors on the relationship between local psychological openness and firm innovation. Our empirical investigation of a large and longitudinal sample of Swedish firms across 2004 to 2018 revealed a compensatory effect of local psychological openness for local 'structural knowledge gaps' in less endowed peripheral regions. Implications for research and policymaking addressing innovation in firms and regions are discussed.

4a32a2255e:5d529bbfd2be930a.title: Varieties of innovation and transition pathways in rural areas: A theoretical perspective to technology-, community-, and nature-based development
4a32a2255e:5d529bbfd2be930a.author: Sasso, Simone
4a32a2255e:5d529bbfd2be930a.summary: Rural regions encompass a wide variety of contexts, often facing challenges such as population decline and ageing, or limited infrastructure and services. Yet, rural territories can also be unique places for experimentation and serve as sites of transformative, sustainability-oriented development. We contribute with the development of a theoretical perspective on rural transition pathways that connects rural pre-conditions across industrial, social, and ecological dimensions with distinct varieties of innovation—technological, community-based, and nature-based—and with system effects achieved through two key elements: change agency and rescaling. We identify four archetypes of transition pathways in rural areas: rescaling a rural niche, transforming an existing industry, a community-based pathway, and a nature-based pathway, and provide an empirical illustration for each. The archetypes capture variations of possible transition pathways grounded in theoretical differences in the processes leading to system change. As such, the archetypes are propositions regarding why and how sustainable and inclusive system change can occur in rural regions.

4a32a2255e:a44eebaaf19a861f.title: A geolocated dataset of German news articles
4a32a2255e:a44eebaaf19a861f.author: Losacker, Sebastian
4a32a2255e:a44eebaaf19a861f.summary: The emergence of large language models and the exponential growth of digitized text data have revolutionized research methodologies across a broad range of social sciences. News articles are an important source of digitized text data in this context. News data is crucial for the social sciences as it provides real-time insights into public discourse and societal trends, helping to understand various social phenomena and dynamics. However, most research involving news data is conducted at the national level, as geographically more granular news data is often unavailable. In this paper, we address this gap by providing insights into how news articles can be geolocated and how the texts can then be further analyzed. More specifically, we collect data from the CommonCrawl News dataset and clean the text data for further analysis. We then use a named-entity recognition model for geocoding, linking news articles to geographic locations. Finally, we transform the news articles into text embeddings using SBERT, enabling semantic searches within the news data corpus. In the paper, we apply this process to all German news articles and make the German location data, as well as the embeddings, available for download. As a result, we compile a dataset containing text embeddings for about 50 million German news articles, of which about 70% include geographic locations. The process can be replicated for news data from other countries, as we provide all code and workflows.

4a32a2255e:470c1610b1df621e.title: Human Capital Accumulation Across Space
4a32a2255e:470c1610b1df621e.author: Esteban Rossi-Hansberg
4a32a2255e:470c1610b1df621e.summary: This paper studies how human capital shapes the economic geography of development. We propose a model in which human capital acquisition costs vary across space, and regions with higher human capital invest more in human-capital-augmenting technology. Locations are interconnected through costly migration and trade. Using data on local income and schooling, we quantify the model at a 1° x 1° resolution globally. Over two centuries, the model mostly predicts persistence in the spatial distribution of development. Proportionally lowering education costs in sub-Saharan Africa raises local outcomes but lowers global welfare, while the same policy in Latin America improves global welfare. An alternative policy that equalizes educational costs across sub-Saharan Africa generates worse outcomes, as population shifts within the region toward less productive areas. These results are driven by the estimated negative correlation between education costs and local fundamentals, as well as spatial inefficiencies due to externalities.

4a32a2255e:d999ac0454e37e25.title: Behind the Scenes: Placemaking and Preferential Circulation in the Making of an Innovative Micro-Cluster (Off-Off-Broadway, 1958-1976)
4a32a2255e:d999ac0454e37e25.author: Raphaël Suire
4a32a2255e:d999ac0454e37e25.summary: While the geography of innovation is often studied at the level of city-regions, main conclusions provide only a partial account of the dynamics unfolding within cities. In this article, we examine how a set of proximate organizational sites located within a city comes to foster innovation. Specifically, we study how the placemaking practices of the entrepreneurs who originate these sites shape the localized landscape of resources that innovators mobilize to innovate. Drawing on the historical case of the Off-Off-Broadway theater (1958-1976), we show that these distributed, independent practices embedded an array of non-redundant resources within a small geographical area and, by fostering the patterning of innovators' attendance across proximate venues, cohered into an innovative micro-cluster. Our findings suggest that entrepreneurs who originate such organizational sites play an active role in infrastructuring innovation within cities, with implications for how we understand the spatial organization of innovation.

He said the matter would involve discussions with Senate leadership and that officials would need more information before determining "whether we send something down or not." Zhao and a Binance spokesperson said user funds are safe. The Binance spokesperson said the exchange's security teams are "reviewing all relevant information with urgency." The big picture: If estimates hold up, the suspected Binance hack would be the biggest crypto attack in history. In 2025, North Korea-linked hackers stole about $1.5 billion worth of crypto from the Bybit exchange. The country has turned hacking and scams into an industrial-scale scourge, focusing on crypto heists and a widespread practice of tricking Western companies into hiring North Korean workers . Between the lines : Crypto is a relatively common hacking target, but massive attacks can leave smaller exchanges vulnerable to collapse due to the potential for panicked withdrawals. Binance's size makes it more insulated, March said. "If this happened to any other business…

33e1d7779a:9f8728e73761a0b6.title: Scoop: Dems privately name Texas as most-flippable red state

The big picture: Texas hasn't elected a Democratic senator since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. Democrats thought they'd end the drought in 2018 and let themselves fall for then-Rep. Beto O'Rourke, who lost to Sen. Ted Cruz by 2.6 percentage points. Four years later, O'Rourke tried again to prove a Democrat could win statewide in Texas. 33e1d7779a:f0d8e1dc1d052975.title: Reddit moves to logged-in experience as AI eats search
33e1d7779a:f0d8e1dc1d052975.author: Sara Fischer
33e1d7779a:f0d8e1dc1d052975.summary: Reddit on Thursday said it's moving to become a primarily logged-in experience, marking one of the most significant shifts in its 21-year history. Why it matters: Reddit has long championed the open web. Now, it's pushing to build a more direct relationship with users while also protecting its data from increased scraping in the AI era. Driving the news: In an interview Thursday, Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman said the company is making the change to improve its user experience, bolster its ads business and prevent bots from scraping its proprietary data. Chief operating officer Jen Wong told Axios the move doesn't represent a change in strategy as the company has always focused on building a direct destination. "It's just that in the last 10 years, because our [data] corpus was open, we got a lot of search traffic, so that became part of the equation" but didn't change the company's mission. Zoom in: Huffman expressed confidence that the change would ultimately improve engagement and monetization, even as changes to traditional search continue to impact user growth in the U.S. "When users log in, they spend more time on Reddit, and we can we better know their interests, so we can target ads better," he said. He also noted that the short-term risk is limited because "the vast majority of engagement and over 80% of our monetization comes from our app and logged-in users." In a shareholder letter, Reddit acknowledged that search referral traffic was "down meaningfully in Q3" and said daily users could decline by a "low-double-digit percentage" in Q4 if search referral trends persist. How it works: Reddit will begin testing the fully logged-in experience this quarter outside the U.S. and collect data on the best approach before it rolls out broader changes gradually. Logged-in users can get tailored content, feeds and recommended communities based on their activity and interests, although they can opt out of personalization. The company is still working…

33e1d7779a:9e4e991dc3fda151.title: The bizarre twist shaking up Alaska's Senate race and catching Trump's ire
33e1d7779a:9e4e991dc3fda151.author: Herb Scribner
33e1d7779a:9e4e991dc3fda151.summary: Alaska's tight Senate race is facing a new controversy over two candidates named Dan Sullivan appearing on the ballot — a twist that's drawn attention from President Trump . The big picture: The controversy is adding uncertainty to one of the nation's most competitive Senate contests, with control of Congress on the line in next week's midterm elections. Catch up quick: The New York Times reported this week that Democratic operatives with ties to Mary Peltola's Senate campaign helped recruit a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan to challenge Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan. Trump accused Peltola and Democrats of election fraud and called for criminal prosecution, though the Times did not establish that any laws were broken. Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into Peltola's campaign over the NYT report. House Republicans are also launching an Alaska Senate race probe. Though the presence of two Sullivans in the Senate race has been known for months, the Times' report adds a new wrinkle to a dispute that's already reached the courts. Here's what to know about the controversy. The same-name Senate race controversy The controversy centers on two candidates with nearly identical names appearing on Alaska's Senate ballot: Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan and unaffiliated challenger Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. The ballot will show registered Republican "Sullivan, Dan S." and unaffiliated candidate "Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr." Peltola and Republican Gerald Heikes will also be on the ballot. The challenger initially filed as a Republican but later changed his registration to undeclared. He will appear on the ballot without a party label. Flashback: Concerns about the duplicate names have existed for months. In June, a top Alaskan election official ruled that candidate Daniel J. Sullivan was ineligible to run on the state's primary ballot. The official said she found the candidacy was "filed with a purpose to confuse or mislead and to thereby compromise the…

33e1d7779a:64ce921a4adf8369.title: After losing his majority, Netanyahu tries to delegitimize election results
33e1d7779a:64ce921a4adf8369.author: Barak Ravid
33e1d7779a:64ce921a4adf8369.summary: After his far-right coalition lost 11 seats in the election, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to discredit the results by claiming there was mass voting fraud in Arab communities. Why it matters: Netanyahu appears to be trying to spook the opposition bloc out of cooperating with Arab parties to form a new government. But the opposition is concerned he has an even more ambitious goal: To prevent the results from being certified at all. That would block the swearing in of a new parliament, in which he would lose his majority. Driving the news: Netanyahu and his Likud party started the campaign to delegitimize the Arab vote days before the elections. Half of Netanyahu's social media posts on Election Day cast suspicion on the unprecedented turnout in Arab communities, an apparent attempt to drive his supporters to the polls. Arab voters cast ballots in historic numbers, winning 19 seats between their two parties. On Wednesday, Netanyahu's Likud party issued a statement claiming the "elections were stolen" by the Arab parties through bribes and fraud. Its claims were based on the arrest of three activists from the Arab Ra'am party who were suspected of paying a small number of voters in one of the Arab cities. The Israeli police said there was no evidence to support Likud's claims of a "stolen" election. Behind the scenes: The situation escalated dramatically on Thursday when a letter sent to the director of the Shin Bet domestic security agency was leaked to Israel's Channel 12. It was written by the supreme court judge who heads the Central Elections Committee. The judge ordered the Shin Bet director to immediately investigate suspicions of election interference by foreign countries and submit conclusions within a week. Shortly after the letter leaked, Israeli media outlets identified Qatar as the country in question. The allegation is that it funneled money to one of the Arab parties to propel turnout in their communities. Over the past year,…

33e1d7779a:7de8ac18f2b2d84b.title: Exclusive: How the permitting bill could change the energy landscape
33e1d7779a:7de8ac18f2b2d84b.author: Ben Geman
33e1d7779a:7de8ac18f2b2d84b.summary: Data: Resources for the Future; Note: Central RFF scenario ; Chart: Ben Geman/Axios The Senate permitting plan would cut emissions from power plants in the near term and help keep electricity prices down, a new analysis finds. Why it matters: The study from scholars at Resources for the Future, a nonpartisan think tank, offers some of the most detailed independent modeling yet of the bill 's effects. It will help inform lobbying and advocacy around the bill ahead of a test vote looming on Nov. 9. Driving the news: The analysis models how the bill would affect the power sector compared with current law and policies. Among the findings from its central scenario: It would drive "robust" transmission expansion ( see above ), enabling "use of additional clean energy and existing resources of all types." Overall electricity system costs are an estimated 3.5% to 7% lower each year through 2041 compared to a no-bill baseline, saving over $350 billion total through 2050 in present-value terms. That should translate into lower electricity bills for people, co-author Kevin Rennert tells Axios, though the study does not directly model retail prices. The bill would boost the build-out of renewables, partly enabled by expansion of transmission, with added clean energy displacing fossil fuels even though additions of gas-fired capacity still occur. CO2 from the power sector would initially drop as more coal is edged aside, and then climb over time — but remain below levels projected without the bill. By the numbers: In 2028, there's roughly 60 gigawatts more clean energy capacity on the grid in the study's central outlook compared to a baseline of current law and policy. Data: Resources for the Future; Chart: Ben Geman/Axios The intrigue: The RFF analysis shows how it sees the bill initially pushing power plant emissions downward. Even that eventual upward trend is hardly guaranteed. This kind of study is by definition packed with assumptions and variables that the authors…

33e1d7779a:b3d2ad1af20f4d45.title: Cape Canaveral in its "boom cycle" of launches
33e1d7779a:b3d2ad1af20f4d45.author: Thomas Novelly
33e1d7779a:b3d2ad1af20f4d45.summary: Call it a new Apollo moment: Rocket launches from Cape Canaveral, Florida, are now outpacing those of the Cold War-era space race that first made the launch site famous. Why it matters: U.S. leaders are rushing to grow the number of rocket providers at America's busiest spaceport amid a space and arms race with China. Beijing plans to send a crew to the Moon by 2030 or sooner and is rapidly building up its satellite and rocket fleets. What they're saying: "There's nothing really comparable in the background of my career to what we're experiencing today," Space Force Col. Brian Chatman, the commander of Florida's rocket range, told Axios in an exclusive interview. Behind the scenes: The Cape is busy expanding to meet President Trump's mandate for the nation to support 1,000 annual launches by 2030. Chatman said with all the contractors on base, inspection backups and parking chaos abound. A rundown of some major projects Chatman is overseeing: SpaceX is expanding its footprint on the Cape for its Starship super heavy-lift launchpads.
